title.zh: 卷五 帝紀第五 孝懷帝 孝愍帝
title.en: Volume 5 Annals 5: Emperor Huai; Emperor Min
title.raw: 卷五 帝紀第五 孝懷帝 孝愍帝 Volume 5 Annals 5: Emperor Huai; Emperor Min

sentences.zh: 帝紀第五

translations.literal: Annals, Number Five.
translations.idiomatic: Annals V.

sentences.zh: 孝懷帝

translations.literal: Emperor Huai the Filial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai (the Filial).

sentences.zh: 孝懷皇帝諱熾，字豐度，武帝第二十五子也。

translations.literal: The Filial Emperor Huai had the taboo name Chi, courtesy name Fengdu, and was the twenty-fifth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The Filial Emperor Huai was named Sima Chi, styled Fengdu, the twenty-fifth son of Emperor Wu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 太熙元年，封豫章郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Taixi reign era, he was enfeoffed Prince of Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Taixi 1 (290 CE) he was invested as Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 屬孝惠之時，宗室構禍，帝沖素自守，門絕賓遊，不交世事，專玩史籍，有譽于時。

translations.literal: It fell in the time of Emperor Hui of Jin; the imperial house brought disaster on itself; the emperor was modest and plain and kept to himself, his gate cut off guests and travel, he did not mingle with worldly affairs, devoted himself to perusing historical texts, and had a good reputation in his day.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Hui, as kinsmen of the house tore one another apart, he lived quietly and kept his distance, shut his doors to visitors, took no part in public life, and immersed himself in the histories, winning praise for it at the time.

sentences.zh: 初拜散騎常侍，及趙王倫篡，見收。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; when Prince Zhao Sima Lun usurped the throne, he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: He first received appointment as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; when Sima Lun of Zhao seized power, he was arrested.

sentences.zh: 倫敗，爲射聲校尉。

translations.literal: When Lun was defeated, he became Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot by Sound.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun’s fall he was made Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot by Sound.

sentences.zh: 累遷車騎大將軍、都督青州諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Area Commander of military affairs in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to General of Chariots and Cavalry and area commander over Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未之鎮。

translations.literal: He did not go to that posting.
translations.idiomatic: He never took up the Qingzhou command.

sentences.zh: 光熙元年十一月庚午，孝惠帝崩。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Guangxi, on the day gengwu, Emperor Hui of Jin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Guangxi 1 (306), on gengwu, Emperor Hui died.

sentences.zh: 羊皇后以於太弟爲嫂，不得爲太后，催清河王覃入，已至尚書閣，侍中華混等急召太弟。

translations.literal: Empress Yang, because the Grand Heir-Apparent was her brother-in-law by marriage, could not become empress dowager; she urged Prince Qinghe Sima Tan to enter; he had already reached the Secretariat pavilion; Palace Attendants Hua Hun and others urgently summoned the Grand Heir-Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang could not be styled empress dowager while the heir apparent was her brother-in-law, so she pressed Prince Qinghe, Sima Tan, to come forward; he had already reached the Secretariat offices when Attendants-in-Ordinary such as Hua Hun hurriedly called for the heir apparent instead.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，卽皇帝位，大赦，尊皇后羊氏爲惠皇后，居弘訓宮，追尊所生太妃王氏爲皇太后，立妃梁氏爲皇后。

translations.literal: On guiyou he assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, honored Empress Yang as Empress Hui and installed her in the Hongxun Palace, posthumously honored his birth mother, Consort Wang, as empress dowager, and installed Consort Liang as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou he ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, elevated Empress Yang to the title Empress Hui with residence in Hongxun Palace, gave his late mother Lady Wang the posthumous rank of empress dowager, and made Lady Liang empress.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renwu it was the first day of the month; there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: new moon on renwu; a solar eclipse was observed.

sentences.zh: 己亥，封彭城王植子融爲樂城縣王。

translations.literal: On jihai, the son of Prince Pengcheng Sima Zhi, Rong, was enfeoffed Prince of Lecheng county.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Sima Rong, son of Prince Pengcheng Sima Zhi, was invested as Prince of Lecheng county.

sentences.zh: 南陽王模殺河間王顒于雍谷。

translations.literal: Prince Nanyang Sima Mo killed Prince Hejian Sima Yong at Yonggu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mo of Nanyang put Sima Yong of Hejian to death at Yonggu.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以中書監溫羨爲司徒，尚書左僕射王衍爲司空。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Director of the Secretariat Wen Xian was made Minister of Education, and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Yan was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Wen Xian was appointed Minister of Education and Wang Yan Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 己酉，葬孝惠皇帝于太陽陵。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Emperor Hui of Jin was buried at Taiyang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Emperor Hui was interred at the Taiyang imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 李雄別帥李離寇梁州。

translations.literal: A separate commander of Li Xiong, Li Li, raided Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Li, a lieutenant of Li Xiong, attacked Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永嘉元年春正月癸丑朔，大赦，改元，除三族刑。

translations.literal: In spring, first month of the first year of Yongjia, on guichou it was the new moon; a general amnesty was proclaimed, the reign title was changed, and the punishment of exterminating three generations was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, first month of Yongjia 1 (307): new moon on guichou; general amnesty, new era name, and repeal of the “three clans” extermination penalty.

sentences.zh: 乙太傅、東海王越輔政，殺御史中丞諸葛玫。

translations.literal: On jisi, the Grand Mentor, Prince Sima Yue of Donghai, took charge of government and executed Censor-in-Chief Zhuge Mei.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Grand Mentor Sima Yue of Donghai took the reins of government and had Censor-in-Chief Zhuge Mei put to death.

sentences.zh: 二月辛巳，東萊人王彌起兵反，寇青、徐二州，長廣太守宋羆、東牟太守龐伉並遇害。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinsi, a man of Donglai, Wang Mi, raised troops in rebellion and raided Qing and Xu provinces; Grand Administrator of Changguang Song Pi and Grand Administrator of Dongmou Pang Kang both met violent death.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, xinsi: Wang Mi of Donglai rebelled and struck Qing and Xu; Song Pi of Changguang and Pang Kang of Dongmou were killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 三月己未朔，平東將軍周馥斬送陳敏首。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiwei it was the new moon; General Who Pacifies the East Zhou Fu sent in the head of Chen Min.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, new moon on jiwei: Zhou Fu, General Who Pacifies the East, forwarded Chen Min’s severed head.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，改葬武悼楊皇后。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Empress Wu Dao Yang was reburied.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Empress Yang the Martyr (posthumously “Martial”) was given a second burial.

sentences.zh: 庚午，立豫章王詮爲皇太子。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Prince Yuzhang Sima Quan was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Sima Quan, Prince of Yuzhang, was named heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 辛未，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei a general amnesty was ordered.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，東海王越出鎮許昌。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Prince Sima Yue of Donghai went out to garrison Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Sima Yue of Donghai moved his headquarters to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 以征東將軍、高密王簡爲征南大將軍、都督荊州諸軍事，鎮襄陽；

translations.literal: The General Who Conquers the East, Prince Sima Jian of Gaomi, was made General Who Conquers the South and Area Commander of military affairs in Jingzhou, and stationed at Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jian of Gaomi, General Who Conquers the East, was promoted to General Who Conquers the South, given overall command in Jingzhou, and posted to Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 改封安北將軍、東燕王騰爲新蔡王、都督司冀二州諸軍事，鎮鄴；

translations.literal: Prince Sima Teng of Dongyan, General Who Guards the North, was redesignated Prince of Xincai and Area Commander of military affairs in Si and Ji provinces, and stationed at Ye;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Teng of Dongyan, General Who Guards the North, was transferred to the title Prince of Xincai, given command over Si and Ji, and stationed at Ye;

sentences.zh: 以征南將軍、南陽王模爲征西大將軍、都督秦雍梁益四州諸軍事，鎮長安。

translations.literal: The General Who Conquers the South, Prince Sima Mo of Nanyang, was made General Who Conquers the West and Area Commander of military affairs in Qin, Yong, Liang, and Yi, and stationed at Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mo of Nanyang, General Who Conquers the South, became General Who Conquers the West with command over Qin, Yong, Liang, and Yi, and took up duty at Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 幷州諸郡爲劉元海所陷，刺史劉琨獨保晉陽。

translations.literal: The commanderies of Bingzhou fell to Liu Yuanhai (Liu Yuan); only the Inspector Liu Kun held out at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan’s forces overran Bingzhou; Inspector Liu Kun alone kept a foothold at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，馬牧帥汲桑聚衆反，敗魏郡太守馮嵩，遂陷鄴城，害新蔡王騰。

translations.literal: In summer, fifth month, the horse-herds overseer Ji Sang gathered a host in revolt, defeated Grand Administrator of Wei commandery Feng Song, then took Ye and killed Prince Sima Teng of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fifth month: Ji Sang, overseer of the imperial studs, rebelled, routed Feng Song of Wei, seized Ye, and slew Prince Sima Teng of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 燒鄴宮，火旬日不滅。

translations.literal: He burned the Ye palaces; the fire did not go out for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: The palaces at Ye were set ablaze and burned for ten days straight.

sentences.zh: 又殺前幽州刺史石尟于樂陵，入掠平原，山陽公劉秋遇害。

translations.literal: He also killed the former Inspector of Youzhou Shi Xian at Leling, entered and plundered Pingyuan, and Prince of Shanyang Liu Qiu met violent death.
translations.idiomatic: He also executed former Youzhou inspector Shi Xian at Leling, raided into Pingyuan, and killed Liu Qiu, duke of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 洛陽步廣里地陷，有二鵝出，色蒼者沖天，白者不能飛。

translations.literal: The ground in Buligu ward in Luoyang sank; two geese emerged; the dark-colored one flew up to the sky; the white one could not fly.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang’s Buligu lane the earth opened; two geese emerged—one gray shot skyward while a white one could not leave the ground.

sentences.zh: 建寧郡夷攻陷寧州，死者三千餘人。

translations.literal: The Yi of Jianning commandery attacked and took Ningzhou; more than three thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Yi tribesmen in Jianning overran Ningzhou, leaving over three thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己酉朔，東海王越進屯官渡，以討汲桑。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, on jiyou it was the new moon; Prince Sima Yue of Donghai advanced and encamped at Guandu to campaign against Ji Sang.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, new moon on jiyou: Sima Yue of Donghai marched to Guandu to strike Ji Sang.

sentences.zh: 己未，以平東將軍、琅邪王睿爲安東將軍、都督揚州江南諸軍事、假節，鎮建鄴。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Prince Sima Rui of Langya, who held the title General Who Pacifies the East, was appointed General Who Guards the East, Area Commander of military affairs south of the Yangzi in Yangzhou, given credential axes, and stationed at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Sima Rui of Langye—already a General Who Pacifies the East—was promoted to General Who Guards the East, given command of military affairs in Yangzhou south of the river with ceremonial axes, and posted to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 八月己卯朔，撫軍將軍苟晞敗汲桑於鄴。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jimao it was the new moon; General Who Supports the Army Gou Xi defeated Ji Sang at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, new moon on jimao: Gou Xi, General Who Supports the Army, routed Ji Sang at Ye.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，曲赦幽、幷、司、冀、兗、豫等六州。

translations.literal: On jiachen, a partial amnesty was proclaimed for You, Bing, Si, Ji, Yan, and Yu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen six northern provinces received a selective amnesty.

sentences.zh: 分荊州、江州八郡爲湘州。

translations.literal: Eight commanderies of Jingzhou and Jiangzhou were split off to form Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eight commanderies from Jing and Jiang were carved out as a new Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月戊申，苟晞又破汲桑，陷其九壘。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wushen, Gou Xi again defeated Ji Sang and broke through his nine fortified camps.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, wushen: Gou Xi smashed Ji Sang again and overran his nine stockades.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，有大星如日，小者如斗，自西方流於東北，天盡赤，俄有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On xinhai, there was a large star like the sun and small ones like dippers, flowing from the west toward the northeast; the whole sky turned red; shortly there was a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai enormous meteors—one bright as the sun, others like cups—streaked from west to northeast, reddening the heavens, followed moments later by thunderous noise.

sentences.zh: 始修千金堨於許昌以通運。

translations.literal: They began repairing the Qianjin Weir at Xuchang to open transport.
translations.idiomatic: Work began on the Qianjin diversion weir at Xuchang to ease supply lines.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月戊申朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In winter, eleventh month, on wushen it was the new moon; there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, eleventh month, new moon on wushen: eclipse of the sun.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以尚書右僕射和郁爲征北將軍，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat He Yu was made General Who Conquers the North and stationed at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin He Yu, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, was posted as General Who Conquers the North at Ye.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊寅，幷州人田蘭、薄盛等斬汲桑于樂陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuyin, the Bingzhou men Tian Lan and Bo Sheng and others beheaded Ji Sang at Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, wuyin: Tian Lan, Bo Sheng, and other Bingzhou irregulars executed Ji Sang at Leling.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以前太傅劉寔爲太尉。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the former Grand Mentor Liu Shi was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu former Grand Mentor Liu Shi was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以光祿大夫、延陵公高光爲尚書令。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, Duke of Yanling Gao Guang was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Gao Guang, Grand Master of Splendid Carriage and duke of Yanling, became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 東海王越矯詔囚清河王覃于金墉城。

translations.literal: Prince Sima Yue of Donghai forged an edict and imprisoned Prince Qinghe Sima Tan in the Jincheng fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue of Donghai used a forged rescript to lock Prince Qinghe Sima Tan inside Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，越自爲丞相。

translations.literal: On guimao, Yue made himself Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Yue took the title of chancellor for himself.

sentences.zh: 以撫軍將軍苟晞爲征東大將軍。

translations.literal: Gou Xi, General Who Supports the Army, was made General Who Conquers the East.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi was promoted to General Who Conquers the East.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月丙子朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In spring, first month of the second year, on bingzi it was the new moon; there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, second year of Yongjia, first month, new moon on bingzi: solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丁未，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 二月辛卯，清河王覃爲東海王越所害。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinmao, Prince Qinghe Sima Tan was killed by Prince Sima Yue of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, xinmao: Sima Tan of Qinghe was murdered on Sima Yue of Donghai’s orders.

sentences.zh: 庚子，石勒寇常山，安北將軍王浚討破之。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Shi Le raided Changshan; General Who Guards the North Wang Jun attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Shi Le struck Changshan and was beaten by Wang Jun, General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 三月，東海王越鎮鄄城。

translations.literal: In the third month, Prince Sima Yue of Donghai garrisoned Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: Sima Yue of Donghai shifted his base to Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 劉元海侵汲郡，略有頓丘、河內之地。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanhai invaded Ji commandery and seized territory in Dunqiu and Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan pushed into Ji commandery, overrunning Dunqiu and Henei.

sentences.zh: 王彌寇青、徐、兗、豫四州。

translations.literal: Wang Mi raided Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi ravaged Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁亥，入許昌，諸郡守將皆奔走。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on dinghai, he entered Xuchang; the defending officials of the commanderies all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, dinghai: he broke into Xuchang and every local commander fled.

sentences.zh: 五月甲子，彌遂寇洛陽，司徒王衍帥衆禦之，彌退走。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiazi, Mi then raided Luoyang; Minister of Education Wang Yan led the host to resist him; Mi withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, jiazi: Wang Mi pressed on Luoyang; Minister of Education Wang Yan led the defense and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲辰，劉元海寇平陽，太守宋抽奔京師，河東太守路述力戰，死之。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, on jiachen, Liu Yuanhai raided Pingyang; Grand Administrator Song Chou fled to the capital; Grand Administrator of Hedong Lu Shu fought hard and died.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, jiachen: Liu Yuan struck Pingyang; Song Chou abandoned the city for the capital; Lu Shu of Hedong resisted to the death.

sentences.zh: 八月丁亥，東海王越自鄄城遷屯于濮陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dinghai, Prince Sima Yue of Donghai moved his encampment from Juancheng to Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, dinghai: Sima Yue relocated his army from Juancheng to Puyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，石勒寇趙郡，征北將軍和郁自鄴奔于衛國。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Shi Le raided Zhao commandery; General Who Conquers the North He Yu fled from Ye to Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Shi Le hit Zhao commandery; He Yu, General Who Conquers the North, bolted from Ye toward Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲戌，劉元海僭帝號于平陽，仍稱漢。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, on jiaxu, Liu Yuanhai presumptuously took the imperial title at Pingyang and still called his state Han.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, jiaxu: Liu Yuan declared himself emperor at Pingyang while keeping the dynastic name Han.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙巳，尚書令高光卒；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yisi, Director of the Secretariat Gao Guang died;
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, yisi: Gao Guang, Director of the Secretariat, died;

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以太子少傅荀籓爲尚書令。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent Xun Fan was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Xun Fan, junior tutor to the heir, succeeded him as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 己酉，石勒寇鄴，魏郡太守王粹戰敗，死之。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Shi Le raided Ye; Grand Administrator of Wei commandery Wang Cui was defeated in battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Shi Le assaulted Ye; Wang Cui of Wei commandery fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛未朔，大赦。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinwei it was the new moon; a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, new moon on xinwei: general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 立長沙王乂子碩爲長沙王，尟爲臨淮王。

translations.literal: Sima Shuo, son of Prince Changsha Sima Yi, was established as Prince of Changsha, and Sima Xian as Prince of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shuo, son of the late Prince Changsha Sima Yi, was confirmed as Prince of Changsha, while his brother Sima Xian was invested as Prince of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月甲午，彭城王釋薨。

translations.literal: In spring, first month of the third year, on jiawu, Prince Pengcheng Sima Shi died.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, third year, first month, jiawu: Prince Pengcheng Sima Shi died.

sentences.zh: 三月戊申，征南大將軍、高密王簡薨。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wushen, General Who Conquers the South, Prince Sima Jian of Gaomi, died.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, wushen: Sima Jian of Gaomi, General Who Conquers the South, died.

sentences.zh: 以尚書左僕射山簡爲征南將軍、都尉荊湘交廣等四州諸軍事，司隸校尉劉暾爲尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Shan Jian was made General Who Conquers the South and Area Commander of military affairs in Jing, Xiang, Jiao, and Guang; Metropolitan Commandant Liu Tun was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Jian became General Who Conquers the South with command over Jing, Xiang, Jiao, and Guang; Liu Tun took his old post as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，東海王越歸京師。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Prince Sima Yue of Donghai returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Sima Yue came back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，勒兵人宮，於帝側收近臣中書令繆播、帝舅王延等十餘人，並害之。

translations.literal: On chouhai, he led armed men into the palace and, beside the emperor, seized more than ten persons including Palace Secretariat Director Miao Bo and the emperor’s maternal uncle Wang Yan, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: On chouhai he marched troops into the palace, arrested over a dozen men at the emperor’s side—among them Secretariat Director Miao Bo and the emperor’s uncle Wang Yan—and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，曲赦河南郡。

translations.literal: On bingyin, a partial amnesty was proclaimed for Henan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Henan commandery alone was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，太尉劉寔請老，以司徒王衍爲太尉。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Grand Commandant Liu Shi requested retirement on account of age; Minister of Education Wang Yan was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Liu Shi asked to retire; Wang Yan, Minister of Education, was named Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 東海王越領司徒。

translations.literal: Prince Sima Yue of Donghai held the concurrent post of Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue of Donghai added the portfolio of Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 劉元海冠黎陽，遣車騎將軍王堪擊之，王師敗績於延津，死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanhai invaded Liyang; he sent General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Kan against him; the imperial army was routed at Yanjin, and more than thirty thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan drove on Liyang; Wang Kan, General of Chariots and Cavalry, was sent to stop him but the court army was shattered at Yanjin with over thirty thousand casualties.

sentences.zh: 大旱，江、漢、河、洛皆竭，可涉。

translations.literal: Great drought; the Yangzi, Han, Yellow, and Luo rivers all dried up so that they could be forded on foot.
translations.idiomatic: A terrible drought emptied the Yangzi, Han, Yellow, and Luo until people could wade across.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，左積弩將軍朱誕叛奔於劉元海。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, Zhu Dan, General of the Left Strong Crossbowmen, rebelled and fled to Liu Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month: Zhu Dan, general of the left strong crossbow corps, defected to Liu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 石勒攻陷冀州郡縣百餘壁。

translations.literal: Shi Le attacked and took more than a hundred fortified places in Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le overran more than a hundred walled settlements in Ji province.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊辰，當陽地裂三所，各廣三丈，長三百餘步。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, on wuchen, at Dangyang the earth split in three places, each three zhang wide and more than three hundred paces long.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, wuchen: three great fissures opened at Dangyang, each ten meters across and hundreds of paces long.

sentences.zh: 辛未，平陽人劉芒蕩自稱漢後，誑誘羌戎，僭帝號於馬蘭山。

translations.literal: On xinwei, a man of Pingyang, Liu Mangdang, called himself a descendant of Han, deceived and enticed Qiang and Rong tribesmen, and presumptuously took the imperial title on Mount Malan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Liu Mangdang of Pingyang posed as heir to Han, rallied Qiang and Rong bands, and declared himself emperor on Malan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 支胡五斗叟郝索聚衆數千爲亂，屯新豐，與芒蕩合黨。

translations.literal: The Zhi-Hu elder Wudousou Hao Suo gathered several thousand in revolt, encamped at Xinfeng, and joined forces with Mangdang.
translations.idiomatic: The “five-bushel” chieftain Hao Suo mustered thousands at Xinfeng and allied with Mangdang.

sentences.zh: 劉元海遣子聰及王彌寇上黨，圍壺關。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanhai sent his son Cong and Wang Mi to raid Shangdang and besiege Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan dispatched Liu Cong and Wang Mi against Shangdang and put Huguan under siege.

sentences.zh: 幷州刺史劉琨使兵救之，爲聰所敗。

translations.literal: Inspector of Bingzhou Liu Kun sent troops to relieve them and was defeated by Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou inspector Liu Kun’s relief column was routed by Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 淮南內史王曠、將軍施融、曹超及聰戰，又敗，超、融死之。

translations.literal: Interior Governor of Huainan Wang Kuang, generals Shi Rong and Cao Chao, fought Cong and were again defeated; Chao and Rong died in the action.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kuang of Huainan and generals Shi Rong and Cao Chao clashed with Liu Cong, lost again, and Rong and Chao were killed.

sentences.zh: 上黨太守龐淳以郡降賊。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Shangdang Pang Chun surrendered the commandery to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Chun, grand administrator of Shangdang, yielded the city to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 九月丙寅，劉聰圍浚儀，遣平北將軍曹武討之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingyin, Liu Cong besieged Junyi; General Who Pacifies the North Cao Wu was sent to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, bingyin: Liu Cong invested Junyi; Cao Wu, General Who Pacifies the North, was ordered out against him.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，王師敗績。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the imperial army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the government troops were crushed.

sentences.zh: 東海王越入保京城。

translations.literal: Prince Sima Yue of Donghai entered to defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue of Donghai withdrew into Luoyang to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 聰至西明門，越禦之，戰于宣陽門外，大破之。

translations.literal: Cong reached the Ximing Gate; Yue resisted him and fought outside the Xuanyang Gate, smashing him thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong reached the western Ximing Gate; Yue met him in battle outside Xuanyang Gate and broke his army.

sentences.zh: 石勒寇常山，安北將軍王浚使鮮卑騎救之，大破勒於飛龍山。

translations.literal: Shi Le raided Changshan; General Who Guards the North Wang Jun sent Xianbei cavalry to the rescue and greatly defeated Shi Le at Mount Feilong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le struck Changshan; Wang Jun’s Xianbei horse relieved the town and trounced Shi Le at Mount Feilong.

sentences.zh: 征西大將軍、南陽王模使其將淳于定破劉芒蕩、五斗叟，並斬之。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West, Prince Sima Mo of Nanyang, sent his officer Chunyu Ding to defeat Liu Mangdang and Wudousou and beheaded them both.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mo’s general Chunyu Ding destroyed Liu Mangdang and Hao Suo and sent in their heads.

sentences.zh: 使車騎將軍王堪、平北將軍曹武討劉聰，王師敗績，堪奔還京師。

translations.literal: He ordered General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Kan and General Who Pacifies the North Cao Wu to campaign against Liu Cong; the imperial army was routed; Kan fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kan and Cao Wu were sent against Liu Cong but the court army collapsed; Wang Kan raced back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 李雄別帥羅羨以梓潼歸順。

translations.literal: A separate commander of Li Xiong, Luo Xian, submitted with Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian, another of Li Xiong’s commanders, came over with Zitong commandery.

sentences.zh: 劉聰攻洛陽西明門，不克。

translations.literal: Liu Cong attacked Luoyang’s Ximing Gate but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong assaulted the Ximing Gate of Luoyang without success.

sentences.zh: 宜都夷道山崩，荊、湘二州地震。

translations.literal: At Yidu in Yidao the mountain collapsed; Jing and Xiang provinces suffered earthquakes.
translations.idiomatic: Landslides struck Yidao in Yidu; Jing and Xiang were shaken by earthquakes.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，石勒陷長樂，安北將軍王斌遇害。

translations.literal: In winter, eleventh month, Shi Le took Changle; General Who Guards the North Wang Bin met violent death.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, eleventh month: Shi Le seized Changle and killed Wang Bin, General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 因屠黎陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he massacred the people of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then put Liyang to the sword.

sentences.zh: 乞活帥李惲、薄盛等帥衆救京師，聰退走。

translations.literal: The “Qihuo” survivor chieftains Li Yun and Bo Sheng led their forces to relieve the capital, and Cong withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun and Bo Sheng, leaders of the refugee “Qihuo” bands, marched to lift the siege of Luoyang and forced Liu Cong to pull back.

sentences.zh: 惲等又破王彌于新汲。

translations.literal: Yun and the others again defeated Wang Mi at Xinji.
translations.idiomatic: They routed Wang Mi again near Xinji.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙亥，夜有白氣如帶，自地升天，南北各二丈。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yihai, at night there was white vapor like a belt rising from the ground to the sky, two zhang wide to north and south.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai that winter a pale band of light lifted from earth to sky, about forty feet across from north to south.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月乙丑朔，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, first month of the fourth year, on yichou it was the new moon; a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Spring of the fourth Yongjia year opened with a new moon on yichou and a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二月，石勒襲鄄城，兗州刺史袁孚戰敗，爲其部下所害。

translations.literal: In the second month, Shi Le raided Juancheng; Inspector of Yanzhou Yuan Fu was defeated in battle and killed by his own troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le struck Juancheng in the second month; Yuan Fu, inspector of Yanzhou, lost the fight and was slain by his men.

sentences.zh: 勒又襲白馬，車騎將軍王堪死之。

translations.literal: Le again raided Baima; General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Kan died in the action.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le hit Baima next, and Wang Kan, general of chariots and cavalry, fell there.

sentences.zh: 李雄將文碩殺雄大將軍李國，以巴西歸順。

translations.literal: A general of Li Xiong, Wen Shuo, killed Li Xiong’s grand general Li Guo and brought Ba commandery over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shuo, one of Li Xiong’s commanders, assassinated Li Guo, Li Xiong’s grand general, then turned Ba commandery over to the Jin court.

sentences.zh: 戊午，吳興人錢璯反，自稱平西將軍。

translations.literal: On wuwu, a man of Wuxing, Qian Huang, rebelled and styled himself General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Qian Huang of Wuxing rose in revolt and proclaimed himself General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 三月，丞相倉曹屬周玘帥鄉人討璯，斬之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhou Qi, a clerk in the granary section of the chancellor’s office, led his fellow townsmen against Huang and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Zhou Qi, attached to the chancellor’s granary bureau, rallied local militia, crushed Qian Huang, and took his head.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，大水。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, there were great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Summer brought catastrophic flooding.

sentences.zh: 將軍祁弘破劉元海將劉靈曜于廣宗。

translations.literal: General Qi Hong defeated Liu Yuan’s general Liu Lingyao at Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangzong Qi Hong broke the army of Liu Lingyao, a lieutenant of Liu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 李雄陷梓潼。

translations.literal: Li Xiong took Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong’s forces occupied Zitong.

sentences.zh: 兗州地震。

translations.literal: There was an earthquake in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou was shaken by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 五月，石勒寇汲郡，執太守胡寵，遂南濟河，滎陽太守裴純奔建鄴。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Shi Le raided Ji commandery, seized Grand Administrator Hu Chong, then crossed the Yellow River southward, and Grand Administrator of Xingyang Pei Chun fled to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Shi Le swept through Ji, captured Hu Chong, forded the river south, and drove Pei Chun of Xingyang all the way to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 大風折木。

translations.literal: A great wind broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: A violent gale snapped trees across the region.

sentences.zh: 地震。

translations.literal: There was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: The earth trembled again.

sentences.zh: 幽、幷、司、冀、秦、雍等六州大蝗，食草木，牛馬毛皆盡。

translations.literal: In You, Bing, Si, Ji, Qin, and Yong there was a vast locust plague; they devoured grass and trees until even the hair of cattle and horses was gone.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts swarmed six northern provinces, stripping vegetation bare and even consuming the hair off livestock.

sentences.zh: 六月，劉元海死，其子和嗣偽位，和弟聰殺和而自立。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Liu Yuan died; his son He inherited the usurped throne, and He’s younger brother Cong killed He and set himself up.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan died in the sixth month; his son Liu He briefly held the Han throne until Liu Cong murdered him and seized power.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，劉聰從弟曜及其將石勒圍懷，詔征虜將軍宋抽救之，爲曜所敗，抽死之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Liu Cong’s cousin Liu Yao and his general Shi Le besieged Huai; an edict ordered General Who Conquers the Enemy Song Chou to relieve the city; he was defeated by Yao and died.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Liu Yao and Shi Le invested Huai; Song Chou was sent to break the siege but was crushed by Liu Yao and killed.

sentences.zh: 九月，河內人樂仰執太守裴整叛，降于石勒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, a man of Henei, Le Yang, seized Grand Administrator Pei Zheng in revolt and surrendered to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Le Yang of Henei mutinied, took Pei Zheng hostage, and went over to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 徐州監軍王隆自下邳棄軍奔于周馥。

translations.literal: The army supervisor of Xuzhou, Wang Long, abandoned his command at Xiapi and fled to Zhou Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Long, Xuzhou’s overseer of troops, threw away his army at Xiapi and ran to Zhou Fu.

sentences.zh: 雍州人王如舉兵反于宛，殺害令長，自號大將軍、司雍二州牧，大掠漢沔，新平人龐寔、馮翊人嚴嶷、京兆人侯脫等各起兵應之。

translations.literal: A man of Yongzhou, Wang Ru, raised troops in revolt at Wan, murdered magistrates, styled himself grand general and shepherd of Si and Yong, plundered the Han and Mian valleys, and the men Pang Shi of Xinping, Yan Yi of Fengyi, and Hou Tuo of Jingzhao each raised forces in response.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru of Yongzhou rebelled at Wan, slaughtered local officials, declared himself grand general and governor of Si and Yong, ravaged the Han River basin, while Pang Shi, Yan Yi, and Hou Tuo rose in support from neighboring commanderies.

sentences.zh: 征南將軍山簡、荊州刺史王澄、南中郎將杜蕤並遣兵援京師，及如戰于宛，諸軍皆大敗；

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the South Shan Jian, Inspector of Jingzhou Wang Cheng, and General of the Center Du Rui all sent troops to aid the capital; they fought Wang Ru at Wan and were utterly routed;
translations.idiomatic: Shan Jian, Wang Cheng, and Du Rui dispatched relief columns toward Luoyang, only to meet disaster at Wan against Wang Ru;

sentences.zh: 王澄獨以衆進至沶口，衆潰而歸。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng alone advanced with his host to the mouth of the Yi River; his army broke and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: only Wang Cheng pushed on as far as the Yi ford before his men collapsed and he retreated alone.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛卯，晝昏，至於庚子。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinmao, daylight remained dim from that day until gengzi.
translations.idiomatic: From xinmao through gengzi in the tenth winter month the sky stayed unnaturally dark at noon.

sentences.zh: 大星西南墜，有聲。

translations.literal: A large star fell toward the southwest; there was a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: A huge meteor streaked southwest with a thunderous roar.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，石勒圍倉垣，陳留內史王贊擊敗之，勒走河北。

translations.literal: On renyin, Shi Le besieged Cangyuan; Interior Governor of Chenliu Wang Zan attacked and defeated him, and Le fled north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Wang Zan of Chenliu drove Shi Le away from Cangyuan and sent him fleeing north of the river.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以驃騎將軍王浚爲司空，平北將軍劉琨爲平北大將軍。

translations.literal: On renzi, General of Agile Cavalry Wang Jun was made Minister of Works, and General Who Pacifies the North Liu Kun was promoted to grand general with the same pacification title.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Wang Jun was named Minister of Works while Liu Kun was elevated to grand general still charged with guarding the north.

sentences.zh: 京師饑。

translations.literal: There was famine in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 東海王越羽檄徵天下兵，帝謂使者曰：「爲我語諸征鎮，若今日，尚可救，後則無逮矣。

translations.literal: Prince Sima Yue of Donghai issued feathered dispatches to levy troops from the realm; the emperor told the messenger, “Go tell every commander on the borders: if they come today the situation can still be saved; later will be too late.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue called up the empire by urgent courier; the emperor sent word through the envoy, “Tell the regional commanders that if they march now we may yet be saved—wait, and they will arrive too late.”

sentences.zh: 」時莫有至者。

translations.literal: At that time none arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Not one of them came.

sentences.zh: 石勒陷襄城，太守崔曠遇害，遂至宛。

translations.literal: Shi Le took Xiangcheng; Grand Administrator Cui Kuang was killed; he then advanced to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le seized Xiangcheng, executed Cui Kuang, and pressed on to Wan.

sentences.zh: 王浚遣鮮卑文鴦帥騎救之，勒退。

translations.literal: Wang Jun sent the Xianbei commander Wen Yang at the head of cavalry to relieve the city, and Le withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun detached Wen Yang’s Xianbei horse to the rescue, and Shi Le drew off.

sentences.zh: 浚又遣別將王申始討勒于汶石津，大破之。

translations.literal: Jun also sent a separate commander, Wang Shenshi, to attack Le at the Wenshi ford and inflicted a heavy defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shenshi was sent to ambush Shi Le at the Wenshi crossing and broke his army there.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲戌，東海王越帥衆出許昌，以行臺自隨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiaxu, Prince Sima Yue of Donghai led his host out of Xuchang and took a field headquarters with him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Sima Yue marched out of Xuchang at the head of the army, mobile secretariat in tow.

sentences.zh: 宮省無復守衛，荒饉日甚，殿內死人交橫，府寺營署並掘塹自守，盜賊公行，枹鼓之音不絕。

translations.literal: The palace precincts no longer had defenders; famine grew worse by the day; corpses lay piled in the halls; government bureaus and camps all dug moats to protect themselves; banditry was open in the streets; the sound of watch-drums never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial compound was left undefended, starvation deepened until the corridors filled with the dead, every yamen threw up its own earthworks, robbery ruled the avenues, and alarm drums beat without pause.

sentences.zh: 越軍次項，自領豫州牧，以太尉王衍爲軍司。

translations.literal: Yue’s army halted at Xiang; he personally took the title shepherd of Yuzhou and appointed Grand Commandant Wang Yan chief of staff for the army.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue stopped at Xiang, claimed the Yuzhou governorship for himself, and put Grand Commandant Wang Yan in charge of staff work for the expedition.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，流氐隗伯等襲宜都，太守嵇晞奔建鄴。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the floating Di chieftain Kui Bo and others raided Yidu; Grand Administrator Ji Xi fled to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Kui Bo’s refugee Di band struck Yidu, forcing Grand Administrator Ji Xi to escape to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 王申始攻劉曜、王彌于瓶壘，破之。

translations.literal: Wang Shenshi attacked Liu Yao and Wang Mi at the Ping stockade and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ping redoubt Wang Shenshi turned back Liu Yao and Wang Mi.

sentences.zh: 鎮東將軍周馥表迎大駕遷都壽陽，越使裴碩討馥，爲馥所敗，走保東城，請救于琅邪王睿。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the East Zhou Fu submitted a memorial urging the court to welcome the imperial carriage to a new capital at Shouyang; Yue sent Pei Shuo against Zhou Fu; Shuo was defeated by Fu, fled to hold the east wall, and begged aid from Prince Sima Rui of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu, general who guarded the east, asked to move the throne to Shouyang; Sima Yue answered by sending Pei Shuo, who was beaten, penned in the eastern enceinte, and forced to appeal to Sima Rui of Langya for rescue.

sentences.zh: 襄陽大疫，死者三千餘人。

translations.literal: A great pestilence struck Xiangyang; more than three thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Plague ravaged Xiangyang, killing over three thousand people.

sentences.zh: 加涼州刺史張軌安西將軍。

translations.literal: Inspector of Liangzhou Zhang Gui was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, inspector of Liangzhou, received the added rank of General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 十二月，征東大將軍苟晞攻王彌別帥曹嶷，破之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Grand General Who Conquers the East Gou Xi attacked Wang Mi’s lieutenant Cao Yi and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Gou Xi smashed Cao Yi, a subordinate of Wang Mi.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，平陽人李洪帥流人入定陵作亂。

translations.literal: On yiyou, a man of Pingyang, Li Hong, led displaced people into Dingling and raised a disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Li Hong of Pingyang marched landless refugees into Dingling and stirred revolt there.

sentences.zh: 二月，石勒寇汝南，汝南王祐奔建鄴。

translations.literal: In the second month, Shi Le raided Runan; Prince Runan Sima You fled to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le struck Runan in the second month and drove Prince Runan Sima You south to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 三月戊午，詔下東海王越罪狀，告方鎮討之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuwu, an edict was issued listing the crimes of Prince Sima Yue of Donghai and ordering the regional commanders to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu an edict denounced Sima Yue of Donghai and summoned the provinces to move against him.

sentences.zh: 以證東大將軍苟晞爲大將軍。

translations.literal: Grand General Who Conquers the East Gou Xi was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi, already grand general who conquered the east, was promoted to supreme field command over the loyalist armies.

sentences.zh: 丙子，東海王越薨。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Prince Sima Yue of Donghai died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Sima Yue of Donghai died—on campaign, away from the capital.

sentences.zh: 四月戊子，石勒追東海王越喪，及於東郡，將軍錢端戰死，軍潰，太尉王衍、吏部尚書劉望、廷尉諸葛銓、尚書鄭豫、武陵王澹等皆遇害，王公已下死者十餘萬人。

translations.literal: On wuzi in the fourth month, Shi Le pursued the funeral train of Prince Sima Yue of Donghai, overtook it in Dong commandery, General Qian Duan died in battle, the army was routed, and Grand Commandant Wang Yan, Minister of Personnel Liu Wang, Minister of Justice Zhuge Quan, Director Zheng Yu, Prince Wuling Sima Dan, and others were all killed; among princes, dukes, and below more than a hundred thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Shi Le ran down Sima Yue’s burial cortège in Dong commandery, shattered the escort at the cost of Qian Duan’s life, and slaughtered Wang Yan, Liu Wang, Zhuge Quan, Zheng Yu, Prince Wuling, and hosts of nobles—well over a hundred thousand dead in all.

sentences.zh: 東海世子毗及宗室四十八王尋又沒于石勒。

translations.literal: The heir of Donghai, Pi, and forty-eight princes of the imperial house soon afterward also fell into Shi Le’s hands.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Pi, Yue’s heir, and forty-eight imperial princes were rounded up by Shi Le soon after.

sentences.zh: 賊王桑、冷道陷徐州，刺史裴盾遇害，桑遂濟淮，至於歷陽。

translations.literal: The bandits Wang Sang and Leng Dao took Xuzhou; Inspector Pei Dun was killed; Sang then crossed the Huai and reached Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sang and Leng Dao overran Xuzhou, murdered Pei Dun, crossed the Huai, and advanced on Liyang.

sentences.zh: 五月，益州流人汝班、梁州流人蹇撫作亂于湘州，虜刺史苟眺，南破零、桂諸郡，東掠武昌，安城太守郭察、劭陵太守鄭融、衡陽內史滕育並遇害。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the displaced men Ru Ban of Yizhou and Jian Fu of Liangzhou raised a revolt in Xiangzhou, captured Inspector Gou Tiao, broke south through the Ling and Gui commanderies, plundered east to Wuchang, and Grand Administrator of Ancheng Guo Cha, Grand Administrator of Shaoling Zheng Rong, and Interior Governor of Hengyang Teng Yu were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Ru Ban and Jian Fu, refugees from Yi and Liang, mutinied in Xiangzhou, seized Gou Tiao, swept through the southern counties, raided Wuchang, and killed Guo Cha, Zheng Rong, and Teng Yu.

sentences.zh: 進司空王浚爲大司馬，征西大將軍、南陽王模爲太尉，太子太傅傅祗爲司徒，尚書令荀籓爲司空，安東將軍、琅邪王睿爲鎮東大將軍。

translations.literal: Wang Jun was advanced from Minister of Works to Grand Marshal; Grand General Who Conquers the West, Prince Sima Mo of Nanyang, was made Grand Commandant; Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent Fu Zhi was made Minister of Education; Director of the Secretariat Xun Fan was made Minister of Works; General Who Guards the East, Prince Sima Rui of Langya, was made Grand General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun became grand marshal, Sima Mo grand commandant, Fu Zhi minister of education, Xun Fan minister of works, and Sima Rui of Langya grand general who guarded the east.

sentences.zh: 東海王越之出也，使河南尹潘滔居守。

translations.literal: When Prince Sima Yue of Donghai went out on campaign, he had Grand Administrator of Henan Pan Tao remain to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, Sima Yue had left Pan Tao, Henan’s governor, to hold Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 大將軍苟晞表遷都倉垣，帝將從之，諸大臣畏滔，不敢奉詔，且宮中及黃門戀資財，不欲出。

translations.literal: Grand General Gou Xi memorialized that the capital be moved to Cangyuan; the emperor was about to consent, but the great ministers feared Pan Tao and dared not carry out the edict, and those inside the palace and the yellow-gate attendants clung to their goods and were unwilling to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi urged relocation to Cangyuan; the emperor was inclined to agree, yet high officials, intimidated by Pan Tao, stalled the order while eunuchs and palace staff hoarded treasure and refused to budge.

sentences.zh: 至是饑甚，人相食，百官流亡者十八九。

translations.literal: By then the famine was extreme; people ate one another; eighteen or nineteen out of ten hundred officials had fled in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Starvation turned to cannibalism; nine officials in ten had already fled the city.

sentences.zh: 帝召羣臣會議，將行而警衛不備。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the ministers in council and was about to set out, but the guard force was not prepared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called a council to depart, only to find no escort ready.

sentences.zh: 帝撫手歎曰：「如何會無車輿！

translations.literal: The emperor clapped his hands and sighed, “How can it be that at a court gathering there are no carriages?”
translations.idiomatic: He wrung his hands and cried, “Is there truly not a single carriage for the Son of Heaven?”

sentences.zh: 」乃使司徒傅祗出詣河陰，修理舟楫，爲水行之備，朝士數人導從。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Minister of Education Fu Zhi to go out to Heyin to repair boats and prepare for travel by water; several courtiers went as guides and escort.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fu Zhi downriver to Heyin to fit out boats while a handful of ministers went ahead as escort.

sentences.zh: 帝步出西掖門。

translations.literal: The emperor walked out through the west side gate of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He then left on foot by the western postern of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 至銅馳街，爲盜所掠，不得進而還。

translations.literal: When he reached Tongtuo Street he was robbed by bandits and could not go forward, so he returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongtuo Street robbers stripped the party; unable to press on, he turned back.

sentences.zh: 六月癸未，劉曜、王彌、石勒同寇洛川，王師頻爲賊所敗，死者甚衆。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guiwei, Liu Yao, Wang Mi, and Shi Le together raided the Luo River region; the imperial army was repeatedly defeated by the rebels and very many died.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the three warlords struck the Luoyang basin and shattered every Jin force sent against them.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，司空荀籓、光祿大夫荀組奔轘轅，太子左率溫幾夜開廣莫門奔小平津。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Minister of Works Xun Fan and Grand Master of Splendid Carriage Xun Zu fled toward Huanyuan; the crown prince’s left guard commander Wen Ji opened the Guangmo Gate by night and fled to Xiaoping ford.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the Xun brothers bolted for Huanyuan while Wen Ji broke out through Guangmo Gate under cover of dark toward Xiaoping ford.

sentences.zh: 丁酉、劉曜、王彌入京師。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Liu Yao and Wang Mi entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Liu Yao and Wang Mi poured into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝開華林園門，出河陰藕池，欲幸長安，爲曜等所追及。

translations.literal: The emperor opened the gate of the Hualin Garden, went out to the lotus pool at Heyin, intended to go to Chang’an, and was overtaken by Yao and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor slipped out through Hualin Garden toward the Heyin lotus pools, hoping to reach Chang’an, but Liu Yao’s riders caught him.

sentences.zh: 曜等遂焚燒宮廟，逼辱妃后，吳王晏、竟陵王楙、尚書左僕射和郁、右僕射曹馥、尚書閭丘沖、袁粲、王緄、河南尹劉默等皆遇害，百官士庶死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Yao and the others then burned the palaces and ancestral shrines, outraged the consorts and empresses, and Prince Wu Sima Yan, Prince Jingling Sima Mao, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat He Yu, Right Vice Director Cao Fu, Director Lüqiu Chong, Yuan Can, Wang Kun, Grand Administrator of Henan Liu Mo, and others were all killed; more than thirty thousand among officials, gentry, and commoners died.
translations.idiomatic: They fired the palaces and temples, violated the women of the harem, and cut down Prince Wu, Prince Jingling, He Yu, Cao Fu, Lüqiu Chong, Yuan Can, Wang Kun, Liu Mo, and tens of thousands more.

sentences.zh: 帝蒙塵于平陽，劉聰以帝爲會稽公。

translations.literal: The emperor suffered the “dust of exile” at Pingyang; Liu Cong made the emperor Duke of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: The captive sovereign was marched to Pingyang, where Liu Cong humiliated him with the title duke of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 荀籓移檄州鎮，以琅邪王爲盟主。

translations.literal: Xun Fan circulated a proclamation to the provinces and commanderies, naming Prince Sima Rui of Langya covenant leader.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Fan’s call to arms recognized Sima Rui of Langya as head of the alliance.

sentences.zh: 豫章王端東奔苟晞，晞立爲皇太子，自領尚書令，具置官屬，保梁國之蒙縣。

translations.literal: Prince Yuzhang Sima Duan fled east to Gou Xi; Xi established him as crown prince, personally took the post of Director of the Secretariat, fully set up offices, and protected himself at Meng county in Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuzhang Sima Duan reached Gou Xi, who enthroned him as a rival heir, assumed the directorate of the secretariat himself, built a full bureaucracy, and entrenched at Meng in Liang.

sentences.zh: 百姓饑儉，米斛萬餘價。

translations.literal: The common people were starving; the price of a hu of grain exceeded ten thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Grain sold for more than ten thousand cash a hu as the people starved.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，大司馬王浚承制假立太子，置百官，署征鎮。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Grand Marshal Wang Jun, acting under interim authority, installed a crown prince, set up the hundred offices, and appointed commanders for conquest and garrison.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wang Jun used emergency powers to name a crown prince and staff a shadow court with regional commands.

sentences.zh: 石勒寇穀陽，沛王滋戰敗遇害。

translations.literal: Shi Le raided Guyang; Prince Pei Sima Zi was defeated in battle and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le attacked Guyang and killed Prince Pei Sima Zi in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 八月，劉聰使子粲攻陷長安，太尉、征西將軍、南陽王模遇害，長安遺人四千餘家奔漢中。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Liu Cong sent his son Can to take Chang’an; Grand Commandant and General Who Conquers the West, Prince Sima Mo of Nanyang, was killed; more than four thousand surviving households of Chang’an fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can stormed Chang’an in the eighth month, slew Sima Mo, and sent four thousand refugee households streaming into Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 九月癸亥，石勒襲陽夏，至於蒙縣，大將軍苟晞、豫章王端並沒于賊。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guihai, Shi Le raided Yangxia, advanced as far as Meng county, and Grand General Gou Xi and Prince Yuzhang Sima Duan both fell into the hands of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Shi Le swept through Yangxia to Meng, capturing Gou Xi and Prince Yuzhang alive.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，勒寇豫州，諸軍至江而還。

translations.literal: In the winter tenth month, Le raided Yuzhou; the various armies reached the Yangzi and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Shi Le probed Yuzhou and withdrew his columns only when they neared the great river.

sentences.zh: 十一月，猗盧寇太原，平北將軍劉琨不能制，徙五縣百姓於新興，以其地居之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yilu raided Taiyuan; General Who Pacifies the North Liu Kun could not stop him and moved the commoners of five counties into Xinxing, settling them on that land.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu struck Taiyuan that eleventh month; unable to hold him, Liu Kun evacuated five counties into Xinxing commandery and resettled the people on Yilu’s old grazing grounds.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月，帝在平陽。

translations.literal: In spring, first month of the sixth year, the emperor was at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth year opened with the emperor still a prisoner at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 劉聰寇太原。

translations.literal: Liu Cong raided Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong renewed his offensive against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 故鎮南府牙門將胡亢聚衆寇荊土，自號楚公。

translations.literal: The former gate guard of the southern garrison headquarters, Hu Kang, gathered a host and raided Jingzhou, styling himself duke of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Kang, once a gate captain on the southern frontier, mustered bandits in Jing and proclaimed himself duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 二月壬子，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on renzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: A solar eclipse fell on renzi in the second month.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，鎮東大將軍、琅邪王睿上尚書，檄四方以討石勒。

translations.literal: On guichou, Grand General Who Guards the East, Prince Sima Rui of Langya, forwarded a memorial to the Secretariat and summoned the four quarters to campaign against Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Sima Rui petitioned Luoyang—still nominally Jin—and called the realm to arms against Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 大司馬王浚移檄天下，稱被中詔承制，以荀籓爲太尉。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wang Jun circulated a proclamation through the realm saying he had received an edict from within the curtains by interim authority and appointed Xun Fan Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun claimed a palace rescript and named Xun Fan grand commandant over the whole north.

sentences.zh: 汝陽王熙爲石勒所害。

translations.literal: Prince Ruyang Sima Xi was killed by Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xi of Ruyang died at Shi Le’s hands.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙寅，征南將軍山簡卒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, General Who Conquers the South Shan Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Shan Jian, general who conquered the south, died.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，歲星、熒惑、太白聚于牛斗。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Jupiter, Mars, and Venus gathered in the Ox and Dipper asterisms.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Jupiter, Mars, and Venus converged on the northern dipper.

sentences.zh: 石勒寇冀州。

translations.literal: Shi Le raided Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le ravaged Ji province again.

sentences.zh: 劉粲寇晉陽，平北將軍劉琨遣部將郝詵帥衆禦粲，詵敗績，死之，太原太守高喬以晉陽降粲。

translations.literal: Liu Can raided Jinyang; General Who Pacifies the North Liu Kun sent his officer Hao Shen with a host to resist Can; Shen was routed and died; Grand Administrator of Taiyuan Gao Qiao surrendered Jinyang to Can.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can besieged Jinyang; Liu Kun’s deputy Hao Shen died in a failed relief; Gao Qiao then handed the city to Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 八月庚戌，劉琨奔于常山。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengxu, Liu Kun fled to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Liu Kun abandoned Taiyuan for Changshan.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，陰平都尉董沖逐太守王鑒，以郡叛降于李雄。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the commandant of Yinping, Dong Chong, drove out Grand Administrator Wang Jian and surrendered the commandery in rebellion to Li Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Dong Chong of Yinping expelled Wang Jian and defected with the commandery to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，劉琨乞師于猗盧，表盧爲代公。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Liu Kun begged troops from Yilu and memorialized Yilu as duke of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: That same xinhai Liu Kun begged cavalry from Yilu and secured him the ducal title over Dai.

sentences.zh: 九月己卯，猗盧使子利孫赴琨，不得進。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jimao, Yilu sent his son Lisun to Kun’s aid but he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Yilu’s son Lisun tried to reach Liu Kun but was blocked on the march.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，前雍州刺史賈疋討劉粲於三輔，走之，關中小定，乃與衛將軍梁芬、京兆太守梁綜共奉秦王鄴爲皇太子於長安。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the former Inspector of Yongzhou, Jia Min, attacked Liu Can in the Three Surrounds region, drove him off, the Guanzhong region was somewhat pacified, and he then together with General of the Guard Liang Fen and Grand Administrator of Jingzhao Liang Zong supported Prince of Qin Sima Ye as crown prince at Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Jia Min, the old Yongzhou inspector, threw back Liu Can around Chang’an; with Liang Fen and Liang Zong he stabilized Guanzhong long enough to enthrone Prince of Qin Sima Ye as heir at the western capital.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，猗盧自將六萬騎次于盆城。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Yilu personally led sixty thousand cavalry and halted at Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu himself led sixty thousand horsemen to a halt at Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲午，劉粲遁走，劉琨收其遺衆，保于陽曲。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiawu, Liu Can fled; Liu Kun gathered his surviving troops and protected himself at Yangqu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Liu Can broke off the siege; Liu Kun collected the wreckage of his army and held Yangqu.

sentences.zh: 是歲大疫。

translations.literal: That year there was a great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: A terrible plague swept the north that year.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月，劉聰大會，使帝著青衣行酒。

translations.literal: In spring, first month of the seventh year, Liu Cong held a great assembly and made the emperor wear blue servants’ robes while pouring wine.
translations.idiomatic: At a New Year banquet Liu Cong forced the Jin emperor to don indigo servant dress and wait on his guests with the wine.

sentences.zh: 侍中庾珉號哭，聰惡之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yu Min wailed aloud; Cong detested it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Min wept at the sight; Liu Cong took offense.

sentences.zh: 丁未，帝遇弑，崩于平陽，時年三十。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the emperor met assassination and died at Pingyang; he was thirty sui.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the captive emperor was murdered at Pingyang at the age of thirty.

sentences.zh: 帝初誕，有嘉禾生于豫章之南昌。

translations.literal: When the emperor was first born, auspicious grain sprouted in Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth a stalk of lucky grain was reported in Nanchang, Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 先是望氣者云「豫章有天子氣」，其後竟以豫章王爲皇太弟。

translations.literal: Earlier a reader of omens had said, “Yuzhang has the qi of a Son of Heaven”; afterward the Prince of Yuzhang indeed became grand heir-apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Court astrologers had long warned that Yuzhang bore imperial omens—omen fulfilled when the prince of that commandery was named grand heir to the throne.

sentences.zh: 在東宮，恂恂謙損，接引朝士，講論書籍。

translations.literal: While in the Eastern Palace, he was modest and self-effacing, received court gentlemen, and discussed books with them.
translations.idiomatic: As heir apparent he lived unassumingly, welcomed officials of the court, and spent his time in conversation over the classics.

sentences.zh: 及卽位，始遵舊制，臨太極殿，使尚書郎讀時令，又於東堂聽政。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he began to follow the old regulations, attended the Taiji Hall, had secretariat gentlemen read the seasonal ordinances, and also heard government business in the eastern hall.
translations.idiomatic: Once emperor he revived precedent: he held audience in the Taiji Hall for the seasonal reading from the calendar, then shifted deliberations to the eastern gallery.

sentences.zh: 至於宴會，輒與羣官論衆務，考經籍。

translations.literal: At banquets he would always debate the myriad tasks of state with the ministers and examine the canonical texts.
translations.idiomatic: Even at feasts he pressed his ministers on policy and tested their learning against the classics.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎傅宣歎曰：「今日復見武帝之世矣！

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Fu Xuan sighed, “Today we see again the age of Emperor Wu!”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan, an attendant at the yellow gates, exclaimed, “It is as if we were back in Emperor Wu’s day!”

sentences.zh: 」秘書監荀崧又常謂人曰：「懷帝天姿清劭，少著英猷，若遭承平，足爲守文佳主。

translations.literal: ” Secretary Supervisor Xun Song also often said to people, “Emperor Huai was clear and keen by nature; in youth he already showed heroic designs; had he met an age of peace, he would have been an excellent ruler who preserved the written pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Song, who oversaw the palace library, would tell anyone who would listen that Sima Chi had been brilliant and disciplined as a young man and would have made a fine conservator on the throne in tranquil times.

sentences.zh: 而繼惠帝擾亂之後，東海專政，無幽厲之釁，而有流亡之禍。」

translations.literal: Yet succeeding after the turmoil of Emperor Hui, with Donghai monopolizing government, there was no crime like that of King You or Li of Zhou, yet there was the calamity of wandering in exile.”
translations.idiomatic: Instead he inherited Hui’s chaos, while Sima Yue of Donghai pulled the strings—no tyranny on the scale of the late Zhou kings, yet the dynasty still stumbled into exile and ruin.”

sentences.zh: 孝愍帝

translations.literal: Emperor Min the Filial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min (the Filial).

sentences.zh: 孝愍皇帝諱鄴，字彥旗，武帝孫，吳孝王晏之子也。

translations.literal: The Filial Emperor Min had the taboo name Ye, courtesy name Yanqi; he was a grandson of Emperor Wu and the son of Prince Wu the Filial, Sima Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The Filial Emperor Min was Sima Ye, styled Yanqi, Emperor Wu’s grandson and the son of Prince Wu the Filial, Sima Yan.

sentences.zh: 出繼後伯父秦獻王柬，襲封秦王。

translations.literal: He went out of the direct line to continue the posterity of his late uncle by seniority, Prince Xian of Qin, Sima Jian, and inherited the enfeoffment as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the succession of his deceased uncle Sima Jian, Prince Xian of Qin, and took the princedom of Qin.

sentences.zh: 永嘉二年，拜散騎常侍、撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongjia, he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Supports the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjia 2 (308) he received the ranks of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and general who supports the army.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽傾覆，避難於滎陽密縣，與舅荀籓、荀組相遇，自密南趨許潁。

translations.literal: When Luoyang collapsed, he took refuge in Mi county in Xingyang commandery, met his maternal uncles Xun Fan and Xun Zu, and hurried south from Mi toward the Xu–Ying region.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Luoyang he fled to Mi in Xingyang, joined his uncles Xun Fan and Xun Zu, and pressed south from Mi toward the Xu–Ying corridor.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史閻鼎與前撫軍長史王毗、司徒長史劉疇、中書郎李昕及籓、組等同謀奉帝歸於長安，而疇等中塗復叛，鼎追殺之，籓、組僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yuzhou Yan Ding, together with the former chief clerk of the army who supports the Army Wang Pi, chief clerk of the Minister of Education Liu Chou, Gentleman of the Secretariat Li Xin, and Xun Fan and Xun Zu, jointly plotted to escort the emperor west to Chang’an; but Chou and others midway rebelled again; Ding pursued and killed them; Fan and Zu barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding of Yuzhou, Wang Pi, Liu Chou, Li Xin, and the two Xuns agreed to shepherd the throne to Chang’an; Liu Chou’s faction turned on them en route, Yan Ding ran them down and executed them, and only the Xun brothers got away.

sentences.zh: 鼎遂挾帝乘牛車，自宛趣武關，頻遇山賊，士卒亡散，次于藍田。

translations.literal: Ding then seized the emperor, riding in an ox-cart, hurried from Wan toward Wu Pass, repeatedly encountered mountain bandits, soldiers scattered and were lost, and halted at Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding then bundled the sovereign into an ox-cart, struck out from Wan for Wu Pass through repeated ambushes until his escort melted away and they stalled at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 鼎告雍州刺史賈疋，疋遽遣州兵迎衛，達于長安，又使輔國將軍梁綜助守之。

translations.literal: Ding informed Inspector of Yongzhou Jia Min; Min immediately sent provincial troops to welcome and guard him until they reached Chang’an, and also sent General Who Supports the State Liang Zong to assist in defending it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding sent word to Jia Min of Yongzhou, who rushed troops to convoy them into Chang’an and detached Liang Zong to stiffen the garrison.

sentences.zh: 時有玉龜出霸水，神馬鳴城南焉。

translations.literal: At that time a jade tortoise came forth in the Ba River, and a spirit horse neighed south of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Portents attended their arrival: a jade tortoise rose from the Ba waters and a “spirit” horse screamed below the southern ramparts.

sentences.zh: 六年九月辛巳，奉秦王爲皇太子，登壇告類，建宗廟社稷，大赦。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, ninth month, on xinsi, they elevated the Prince of Qin as crown prince, ascended the altar to announce the sacrifice to Heaven, established the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, ninth month, xinsi: Prince of Qin Sima Ye was proclaimed heir apparent, the suburban altar rites were performed, the dynastic temple and earth altars were founded, and a general amnesty followed.

sentences.zh: 加疋征西大將軍，以秦州刺史、南陽王保爲大司馬。

translations.literal: Min was additionally appointed Grand General Who Conquers the West; Inspector of Qinzhou, Prince Sima Bao of Nanyang, was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Min was promoted to grand general who conquers the west, while Sima Bao of Nanyang, inspector of Qinzhou, became grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 賈疋討賊張連，遇害，衆推始平太守麹允領雍州刺史，爲盟主，承制選置。

translations.literal: Jia Min campaigned against the bandit Zhang Lian and met violent death; the host pushed Grand Administrator of Shiping Qu Yun to act as Inspector of Yongzhou and covenant leader, acting under interim authority to select and appoint officials.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Min died fighting Zhang Lian’s band; the survivors made Qu Yun of Shiping provisional inspector of Yongzhou and league chief with full powers to fill offices.

sentences.zh: 五月壬辰，以鎮東大將軍、琅邪王睿爲侍中、左丞相、大都督陝東諸軍事，大司馬、南陽王保爲右丞相、大都督陝西諸軍事。

translations.literal: On renchen in the fifth month, Grand General Who Guards the East, Prince Sima Rui of Langya, was made Palace Attendant, Left Chancellor, and Commander-in-chief of all military affairs east of the Shan pass; Grand Marshal, Prince Sima Bao of Nanyang, was made Right Chancellor and Commander-in-chief of all military affairs west of the Shan pass.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Sima Rui of Langya became palace attendant, left chancellor, and supreme commander for everything east of the passes, while Sima Bao of Nanyang became right chancellor and supreme commander for the west.

sentences.zh: 又詔二王曰：「夫陽九百六之災，雖在盛世，猶或遘之。

translations.literal: An edict also said to the two princes, “The disaster of the ‘yang nine, hundred six’ cycle, even in a flourishing age, may still be encountered.
translations.idiomatic: A paired rescript told both men that even golden ages can suffer the cosmic “nine hundred six” catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 朕以幼沖，纂承洪緒，庶憑祖宗之靈，羣公義士之力，蕩滅凶寇，拯拔幽宮，瞻望未達，肝心分裂。

translations.literal: I, being young and tender, have inherited the great line; I hoped to rely on the spirits of the ancestors and the strength of you loyal gentlemen to sweep away the fierce bandits, rescue the secluded palace, yet gazing afar I have not attained it, and my liver and heart are torn apart.
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor avowed his youth, invoked the ancestors, and begged the ministers to destroy the invaders and bring back the captive court from Pingyang—goals still unrealized and heartbreaking.

sentences.zh: 昔周邵分陝，姬氏以隆；

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao divided their rule at Shan, and the House of Ji thereby flourished;
translations.idiomatic: The edict recalled how the Zhou dukes split the realm at the passes and the Ji line prospered;

sentences.zh: 平王東遷，晉鄭爲輔。

translations.literal: King Ping moved east, and Jin and Zheng were his supports.
translations.idiomatic: how King Ping’s eastward move relied on Jin and Zheng as pillars.

sentences.zh: 今左右丞相茂德齊聖，國之昵屬，當恃二公，掃除鯨鯢，奉迎梓宮，克復中興。

translations.literal: Now the left and right chancellors are of abundant virtue, equal in sageliness, intimate kin of the state; I must rely on you two dukes to sweep away the great whales and crocodiles, welcome back the imperial catafalque, and achieve restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Now both chancellors were kinsmen of rare virtue who must scour the realm of rebels, recover the late emperor’s bier, and complete the restoration.

sentences.zh: 令幽、幷兩州勒卒三十萬，直造平陽。

translations.literal: Order You and Bing provinces to press three hundred thousand picked troops straight on Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: You and Bing were to drive three hundred thousand veterans straight at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 右丞相宜帥秦、涼、梁、雍武旅三十萬，徑詣長安。

translations.literal: The right chancellor should lead three hundred thousand warriors from Qin, Liang, Liang, and Yong and go straight to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: The right chancellor was to lead three hundred thousand troops from Qin, Liang, Liang, and Yong straight to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 左丞相帥所領精兵二十萬，徑造洛陽。

translations.literal: The left chancellor should lead two hundred thousand crack troops from his command straight on Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The left chancellor would take two hundred thousand elite troops of his own command toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 分遣前鋒，爲幽幷後駐。

translations.literal: Dispatch vanguard forces to serve as the rear guard for You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard units would cover the rear of the northern thrust.

sentences.zh: 赴同大限，克成元勳。」

translations.literal: All shall answer the same great deadline and together complete the founding merit.”
translations.idiomatic: All were to strike on the same timetable and share the glory of renewal.”

sentences.zh: 又詔琅邪王曰：「朕以沖昧，纂承洪緒，未能梟夷凶逆，奉迎梓宮，枕戈煩冤，肝心抽裂。

translations.literal: An edict also said to the Prince of Langya, “I, being young and ignorant, have inherited the great line; I have been unable to behead and pacify the fierce rebels and welcome the imperial catafalque; sleeping on a spear, vexed and resentful, my liver and heart are torn out.
translations.idiomatic: A separate message to Sima Rui confessed the throne’s helpless youth and shame at failing to ransom Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 前得魏浚表，知公帥先三軍，已據壽春，傳檄諸侯，協齊威勢，想今漸進，已達洛陽。

translations.literal: Earlier I received the memorial of Wei Jun, knowing that you, sir, have led the three armies in advance, already occupy Shouchun, have circulated proclamations to the feudal lords, and coordinated your awesome power; I imagine that by now you have gradually advanced and already reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It cited Wei Jun’s report that Sima Rui had seized Shouchun, issued calls to the provinces, and was thought to be nearing Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史張軌，乃心王室，連旗萬里，已到洴隴；

translations.literal: Inspector of Liangzhou Zhang Gui turns his heart to the royal house; his banners stretch ten thousand li and have already reached Pinglong;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui of Liangzhou, it said, had marched his standards clear across the northwest to the Ping–Long frontier;

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史張光，亦遣巴漢之卒，屯在駱谷：秦川驍勇，其會如林。

translations.literal: Inspector of Liangzhou Zhang Guang has also sent Ba and Han troops encamped at Luogu; the brave men of the Qin plain assemble like a forest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang of Liangzhou had stacked Ba and Han soldiers in the Luogu defile, while Qin’s warriors gathered thick as trees.

sentences.zh: 間遣使適還，具知平陽定問，云幽幷隆盛，餘胡衰破，然猶恃險，當須大舉。

translations.literal: I recently sent envoys who have returned and fully know the settled news from Pingyang, saying You and Bing are flourishing and the remaining Hu are broken, yet they still rely on defiles and will require a great campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh couriers from Pingyang reported You and Bing strong while the barbarians weakened but still entrenched—only a major offensive would root them out.

sentences.zh: 未知公今所到，是以息兵秣馬，未便進軍。

translations.literal: I do not know how far you, sir, have now arrived; therefore I have rested the troops and fed the horses, and have not yet ordered the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Without knowing Sima Rui’s exact position, Chang’an had held its own army back to rest and fodder the horses.

sentences.zh: 今爲已至何許，當須來旨，便乘輿自出，會除中原也。

translations.literal: Now, wherever you have reached, I must await your instruction; then I will personally ride the imperial carriage out to join in clearing the Central Plain.”
translations.idiomatic: Once his location was known, the young emperor would ride out himself to help clear the heartland.”

sentences.zh: 公宜思弘謀猷，勖濟遠略，使山陵旋反，四海有賴。

translations.literal: You, sir, should ponder broad plans and strategies, encourage far-reaching designs, cause the mausoleum hills to turn back [to our possession], and make the four seas have something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Sima Rui to enlarge his strategy so the imperial tombs could be recovered and the empire given hope.

sentences.zh: 故遣殿中都尉劉蜀、蘇馬等具宣朕意。

translations.literal: Therefore I send Palace Commandants Liu Shu, Su Ma, and others fully to announce my intention.
translations.idiomatic: Palace commandants Liu Shu and Su Ma were dispatched to deliver this in full.

sentences.zh: 公茂德昵屬，宣隆東夏，恢融六合，非公而誰！

translations.literal: You, sir, are of abundant virtue, intimate kin, should expand and glorify the eastern summer, and restore harmony to the six directions—if not you, then who!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui, as close kin of proven talent, was told that only he could reunify east and west.

sentences.zh: 但洛都陵廟，不可空曠，公宜鎮撫，以綏山東。

translations.literal: But the mausoleums and temples of the Luoyang capital must not be left empty; you, sir, should pacify and soothe them to quiet the region east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Luoyang’s shrines could not be abandoned, so he must secure the east while

sentences.zh: 右丞相當入輔弼，追蹤周邵，以隆中興也。」

translations.literal: the right chancellor enters to assist at court, following the traces of the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao, in order to make the restoration flourish.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Bao came in as the western pillar to match the Zhou–Shao model of old.”

sentences.zh: 六月，石勒害兗州刺史田徽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Shi Le killed Inspector of Yanzhou Tian Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le executed Tian Hui, inspector of Yanzhou, in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 是時，山東郡邑相繼陷于勒。

translations.literal: At this time commanderies and towns east of the mountains fell one after another into Shi Le’s hands.
translations.idiomatic: One Shandong prefecture after another toppled to Shi Le that season.

sentences.zh: 秋八月癸亥，劉蜀等達于揚州。

translations.literal: In autumn, eighth month, on guihai, Liu Shu and the others reached Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, eighth month, guihai: Liu Shu’s embassy reached Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 改建鄴爲建康，改鄴爲臨漳。

translations.literal: Jianye was renamed Jiankang, and Ye was renamed Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The court renamed Jianye as Jiankang and Ye as Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 杜弢寇武昌，焚燒城邑。

translations.literal: Du Tao raided Wuchang and burned towns.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao torched Wuchang and its suburbs.

sentences.zh: 弢別將王真襲沔陽，荊州刺史周顗奔于健康。

translations.literal: Tao’s lieutenant Wang Zhen raided Mianyang; Inspector of Jingzhou Zhou Yi fled to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen, a lieutenant of Du Tao, struck Mianyang and drove Zhou Yi of Jingzhou east to Jiankang, though the place name in the text is miscopied as a homophone for the usual form Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 九月，司空荀籓薨于滎陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Minister of Works Xun Fan died at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Xun Fan died at Xingyang on the road west.

sentences.zh: 劉聰寇河南，河南尹張髦死之。

translations.literal: Liu Cong raided Henan; Grand Administrator of Henan Zhang Mao died in the action.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong swept Henan and killed Zhang Mao, the capital district’s governor.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，荊州刺史陶侃討杜弢黨杜曾於石城，爲曾所敗。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, Inspector of Jingzhou Tao Kan campaigned against Du Tao’s partisan Du Zeng at Shicheng and was defeated by Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month: Tao Kan of Jingzhou attacked Du Zeng at Shicheng for Du Tao’s faction and lost badly.

sentences.zh: 己巳，大雨雹。

translations.literal: On jisi, there was a great fall of hail.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi hailstones drummed down.

sentences.zh: 庚午，大雪。

translations.literal: On gengwu, there was great snow.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu a blizzard buried the roads.

sentences.zh: 十一月，流人楊武攻陷梁州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the displaced man Yang Wu attacked and took Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: the refugee chief Yang Wu seized Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，河東地震，雨肉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, there was an earthquake in Hedong; it rained flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: Hedong shook and a shower of flesh fell from the sky.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月己巳朔，黑霧著人如墨，連夜，五日乃止。

translations.literal: In spring, first month of the second year, on jisi it was the new moon; black fog clung to people like ink; it continued through the night; after five days it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, spring, new moon on jisi: soot-black mist clung to travelers for five days and nights.

sentences.zh: 辛未，辰時日隕于地。

translations.literal: On xinwei, during the chen double-hour the sun fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei at dawn observers reported the sun “dropping” to earth.

sentences.zh: 又有三日相承，出於西方而東行。
