translations.literal: Moreover there were three suns in succession, coming out in the west and traveling eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Three solar disks were also seen in a line, rising in the west and drifting east.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingchou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou a general amnesty was issued.

sentences.zh: 楊武大略漢中，遂奔李雄。

translations.literal: Yang Wu raided broadly into Hanzhong, then fled to Li Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wu plundered Hanzhong, then defected to Li Xiong in Shu.

sentences.zh: 二月壬寅，以司空王浚爲大司馬，衛將軍荀組爲司空，涼州刺史張軌爲太尉，封西平郡公，幷州刺史劉琨爲大將軍。

translations.literal: On renyin in the second month, Minister of Works Wang Jun was made Grand Marshal, General of the Guard Xun Zu was made Minister of Works, Inspector of Liangzhou Zhang Gui was made Grand Commandant and enfeoffed duke of Xiping, and Inspector of Bingzhou Liu Kun was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, renyin: Wang Jun became grand marshal, Xun Zu minister of works, Zhang Gui grand commandant and duke of Xiping, Liu Kun grand general.

sentences.zh: 三月癸酉，石勒陷幽州，殺侍中、大司馬、幽州牧、博陵公王浚，焚燒城邑，害萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guiyou, Shi Le took Youzhou, killed Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, shepherd of Youzhou, Duke of Boling Wang Jun, burned towns, and harmed more than ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, guiyou: Shi Le overran Youzhou, executed Wang Jun of Boling with his full string of titles, fired the cities, and left ten thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 杜弢別帥王真襲荊州刺史陶侃於林鄣，侃奔灄中。

translations.literal: Du Tao’s lieutenant Wang Zhen raided Inspector of Jingzhou Tao Kan at Linzhang; Kan fled into the Zhen–Han backwaters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen ambushed Tao Kan at Linzhang and chased him into the shallows of the Zhen River, the graph in the text being a variant for the usual river name.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲辰，地震。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on jiachen, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, jiachen: another earthquake.

sentences.zh: 五月壬辰，太尉、領護羌校尉、涼州刺史、西平公張軌薨。

translations.literal: On renchen in the fifth month, Grand Commandant, concurrently Colonel Who Protects the Qiang, Inspector of Liangzhou, Duke of Xiping Zhang Gui died.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, renchen: Zhang Gui died at his post in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，劉曜、趙冉寇新豐諸縣，安東將軍索綝討破之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Liu Yao and Zhao Ran raided the counties around Xinfeng; General Who Guards the East Suo Chen attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: Suo Chen drove Liu Yao and Zhao Ran away from Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，曜、冉等又逼京都，領軍將軍麹允討破之，冉中流矢而死。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, Yao, Ran, and others again pressed the capital region; General Who Commands the Army Qu Yun attacked and defeated them; Ran was hit by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: Qu Yun broke their second thrust on Chang’an; Zhao Ran fell to an arrow.

sentences.zh: 九月，北中郎將劉演克頓丘，斬石勒所署太守邵攀。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, General of the Center Liu Yan took Dunqiu and beheaded Shi Le’s appointed grand administrator Shao Pan.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Liu Yan of the center army recovered Dunqiu and killed Shao Pan, Shi Le’s puppet governor.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，麟見襄平。

translations.literal: On bingxu, a unicorn was seen at Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu a “unicorn” was reported at Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 單于代公猗盧遣使獻馬。

translations.literal: The Chanyu, Duke of Dai Yilu, sent envoys to present horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu, Xiongnu chanyu and duke of Dai, sent tribute horses.

sentences.zh: 蒲子馬生人。

translations.literal: At Puzi a horse gave birth to a person.
translations.idiomatic: At Puzi a mare foaled something shaped like a human child.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月，盜殺晉昌太守趙佩。

translations.literal: In spring, first month of the third year, bandits killed Grand Administrator of Jinchang Zhao Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, spring: robbers murdered Zhao Pei of Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 吳興人徐馥害太守袁琇。

translations.literal: A man of Wuxing, Xu Fu, killed Grand Administrator Yuan Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu of Wuxing assassinated Yuan Xiu, the local governor.

sentences.zh: 以侍中宋哲爲平東將軍，屯華陰。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Song Zhe was made General Who Pacifies the East and encamped at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhe was posted as general who pacifies the east at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 二月丙子，進左丞相、琅邪王睿爲大都督、督中外諸軍事，右丞相、南陽王保爲相國，司空荀組爲太尉，大將軍劉琨爲司空。

translations.literal: On bingzi in the second month, Left Chancellor, Prince Sima Rui of Langya, was advanced to Commander-in-chief and given overall command of all military affairs inside and outside the court; Right Chancellor, Prince Sima Bao of Nanyang, was made chief minister; Minister of Works Xun Zu was made Grand Commandant; Grand General Liu Kun was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, bingzi: Sima Rui took supreme command over every army; Sima Bao became chief minister; Xun Zu and Liu Kun swapped the grand commandant and minister of works portfolios.

sentences.zh: 進封代公猗盧爲代王。

translations.literal: Duke of Dai Yilu was advanced in enfeoffment to King of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu was promoted from duke to king of Dai.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史陶侃破王真於巴陵。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jingzhou Tao Kan defeated Wang Zhen at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan smashed Wang Zhen near Baling.

sentences.zh: 杜弢別將杜弘、張彥與臨川內史謝摛戰于海昏，摛敗績，死之。

translations.literal: Du Tao’s lieutenants Du Hong and Zhang Yan fought Interior Governor of Linchuan Xie Chi at Haihun; Chi was routed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong and Zhang Yan met Xie Chi of Linchuan at Haihun; Xie Chi was killed in the rout.

sentences.zh: 三月，豫率內史周訪擊杜弘，走之，斬張彥於陳。

translations.literal: In the third month, Interior Governor of Yuzhang Zhou Fang attacked Du Hong, drove him off, and beheaded Zhang Yan at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Zhou Fang, interior governor of Yuzhang, routed Du Hong and executed Zhang Yan at Chen.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，大赦。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month: general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五月，劉聰寇幷州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Liu Cong raided Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: Liu Cong struck Bingzhou again.

sentences.zh: 六月，盜發漢霸、杜二陵及薄太后陵，太后面如生，得金玉彩帛不可勝記。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, robbers opened the tombs of Han Emperors Ba and Du and the tomb of Empress Dowager Bo; the empress dowager’s face was as if alive; gold, jade, silks, and brocades obtained were beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: tomb robbers broke into the Western Han mausolea at Ba and Du and Empress Bo’s vault—her corpse seemed lifelike—and looted incalculable treasure.

sentences.zh: 時以朝廷草創，服章多闕，敕收其餘，以實內府。

translations.literal: At the time, because the court was newly founded, robes and insignia were mostly lacking; an edict ordered the collection of the remainder to replenish the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The rump court, starved for regalia, seized what survived of the grave goods for the palace storehouses.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，地震。

translations.literal: On dingmao, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the earth shook.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinsi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi another general amnesty followed.

sentences.zh: 敕雍州掩骼埋胔，修復陵墓，有犯者誅及三族。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yongzhou to gather bones and bury exposed corpses, repair and restore the mausoleums; offenders were to be executed together with three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou was told to gather scattered remains, restore the imperial tombs, and punish tomb raiders with three-clan extermination.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，石勒陷濮陽，害太守韓弘。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, Shi Le took Puyang and killed Grand Administrator Han Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: Shi Le seized Puyang and slew Han Hong.

sentences.zh: 劉聰寇上黨，劉琨遣將救之。

translations.literal: Liu Cong raided Shangdang; Liu Kun sent generals to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong besieged Shangdang while Liu Kun dispatched a relief column.

sentences.zh: 八月癸亥，戰于襄垣，王師敗績。

translations.literal: On guihai in the eighth month, they fought at Xiangyuan; the imperial army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, guihai: the government troops lost a major battle at Xiangyuan.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史陶侃攻杜弢，弢敗走，道死，湘州平。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jingzhou Tao Kan attacked Du Tao; Tao was defeated and fled, died on the road, and Xiangzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan ran Du Tao to ground; Du Tao died fleeing, and Xiangzhou was quieted.

sentences.zh: 九月，劉曜寇北地，命領軍將軍麹允討之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Yao raided Beidi; General Who Commands the Army Qu Yun was ordered to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Liu Yao hit Beidi and Qu Yun was sent to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，允進攻青白城。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, Yun advanced and attacked Qingbai City.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month: Qu Yun pushed on to Qingbai City.

sentences.zh: 以豫州牧、征東將軍索綝爲尚書僕射、都督宮城諸軍事。

translations.literal: Suo Chen, shepherd of Yuzhou and General Who Conquers the East, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Area Commander of military affairs for the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Chen, who governed Yuzhou and held the title general who conquers the east, was named vice director of the secretariat and put in charge of all troops defending the palace enclosure.

sentences.zh: 劉聰陷馮翊，太守梁肅奔萬年。

translations.literal: Liu Cong took Fengyi; Grand Administrator Liang Su fled to Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong overran Fengyi; Liang Su escaped to Wannian.

sentences.zh: 十二月，涼州刺史張寔送皇帝行璽一紐。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Inspector of Liangzhou Zhang Shi sent one cord of the emperor’s traveling seal.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: Zhang Shi forwarded a cord of the mobile imperial seal from Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 盜殺安定太守趙班。

translations.literal: Bandits killed Grand Administrator of Anding Zhao Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Brigands murdered Zhao Ban of Anding.

sentences.zh: 四年春三月，代王猗盧薨，其衆歸于劉琨。

translations.literal: In spring, third month of the fourth year, King of Dai Yilu died; his followers went over to Liu Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, spring, third month: Yilu died; his tribesmen joined Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁丑，劉曜寇上郡，太守籍韋率其衆奔于南鄭。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on dingchou, Liu Yao raided Shang commandery; Grand Administrator Ji Wei led his host and fled to Nanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, dingchou: Liu Yao stormed Shang commandery and Ji Wei led his men south to Nanzhong.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史張寔遣步騎五千來赴京都。

translations.literal: Inspector of Liangzhou Zhang Shi sent five thousand infantry and cavalry to hurry to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi dispatched five thousand foot and horse toward Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 石勒陷廩丘，北中郎將劉演出奔。

translations.literal: Shi Le took Linqiu; General of the Center Liu Yan fled in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le snapped up Linqiu; Liu Yan abandoned his post.

sentences.zh: 五月，平夷太守雷照害南廣太守孟桓，帥二郡三千餘家叛，降于李雄。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Grand Administrator of Pingyi Lei Zhao killed Grand Administrator of Nanguang Meng Huan, led more than three thousand households of the two commanderies in rebellion, and surrendered to Li Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: Lei Zhao of Pingyi slew Meng Huan of Nanguang, then led three thousand families of both districts over to Li Xiong.

sentences.zh: 六月丁巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingsi it was the new moon; there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, new moon on dingsi: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 大蝗。

translations.literal: There was a great locust plague.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts blotted out the countryside.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，劉曜攻北地，麹允帥步騎三萬救之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Liu Yao attacked Beidi; Qu Yun led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: Liu Yao pressed Beidi, and Qu Yun marched thirty thousand men to its relief.

sentences.zh: 王師不戰而潰，北地太守麹昌奔于京師。

translations.literal: The imperial army collapsed without fighting; Grand Administrator of Beidi Qu Chang fled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court army never offered battle; Qu Chang of Beidi bolted for Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 曜進至涇陽，渭北諸城悉潰，建威將軍魯充、散騎常侍梁緯、少府皇甫陽等皆死之。

translations.literal: Yao advanced to Jingyang; all the cities north of the Wei River collapsed; General Who Establishes Might Lu Chong, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Liang Wei, Privy Treasurer Huangfu Yang, and others all died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao pushed to Jingyang, the north-bank towns folded, and Lu Chong, Liang Wei, Huangfu Yang, and their comrades died holding the line.

sentences.zh: 八月，劉曜逼京師，內外斷絕，鎮西將軍焦嵩、平東將軍宋哲、始平太守竺恢等同赴國難，麹允與公卿守長安小城以自固，散騎常侍華輯監京兆、馮翊、弘農、上洛四郡兵東屯霸上，鎮軍將軍胡崧帥城西諸郡兵屯遮馬橋，並不敢進。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Liu Yao pressed the capital; inside and outside were cut off; General Who Guards the West Jiao Song, General Who Pacifies the East Song Zhe, Grand Administrator of Shiping Zhu Hui, and others alike hurried to the national crisis; Qu Yun together with the dukes and ministers defended the small city of Chang’an to hold firm; Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Hua Ji supervised the troops of the four commanderies Jingzhao, Fengyi, Hongnong, and Shangluo and encamped east at Bashang; General Who Guards the Army Hu Song led the troops of the commanderies west of the city and encamped at the Zhema Bridge; yet none dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: Liu Yao tightened the noose on Chang’an. Relief columns under Jiao Song, Song Zhe, and Zhu Hui converged, but Qu Yun and the high ministers could only cling to the inner citadel. Hua Ji camped east at Bashang with four commanderies’ militia, Hu Song blocked the western approaches at Zhema Bridge—and still no one closed with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，京師饑甚，米斗金二兩，人相食，死者太半。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, famine in the capital was extreme; a dou of rice cost two liang of gold; people ate one another; more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: By the tenth winter month grain sold for two liang of gold a dou, cannibalism spread, and well over half the population inside the walls was dead.

sentences.zh: 太倉有麴數餅，麹允屑爲粥以供帝，至是復盡。

translations.literal: The great granary had several cakes of grain; Qu Yun ground them into gruel to supply the emperor; by then it was again exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: A few hard cakes remained in the imperial granary; Qu Yun shaved them into gruel for the throne until even that scrap was gone.

sentences.zh: 帝泣謂允曰：「今窘厄如此，外無救援，死于社稷，是朕事也。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said to Yun, “Now distress is such as this; outside there is no rescue; to die for the altars of soil and grain is my affair.
translations.idiomatic: The boy sovereign wept to Qu Yun: “There is no succor beyond these walls; if I must die for the dynasty, that is my burden alone.”

sentences.zh: 然念將士暴離斯酷，今欲因城未陷爲羞死之事，庶令黎元免屠爛之苦。

translations.literal: Yet I think how cruelly the generals and soldiers have been torn away; now, while the city has not yet fallen, I wish to do the shameful deed of surrender, hoping thereby to let the black-haired people escape the suffering of slaughter and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: “Yet I cannot bear to watch my soldiers ground down further; while a surrender might still spare the people inside, I will accept the shame of yielding before the walls give way.”

sentences.zh: 行矣遣書，朕意決矣。」

translations.literal: Go; dispatch the letter; my mind is decided.”
translations.idiomatic: “Send the letter, then. My decision stands.””

sentences.zh: 十一月乙末，使侍中宋敞送箋于曜，帝乘羊車，肉袒銜壁，輿櫬出降。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yiwei, he had Palace Attendant Song Chang deliver a note to Yao; the emperor rode in a sheep-cart, bared his upper body and held the jade disk in his mouth, and with a bier borne before him went out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei of the eleventh month Song Chang carried his capitulation to Liu Yao; Sima Ye then rode out in the humiliating sheep-cart, shirtless with the surrender jade between his teeth and a coffin carried ahead as token of submission.

sentences.zh: 羣臣號泣攀車，執帝之手，帝亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: The host of ministers wailed, clung to the cart, and grasped the emperor’s hand; the emperor also was overcome with grief.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers sobbed, seized the wheels, and clutched his sleeves until he too broke down.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞吉朗自殺。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor-in-Chief Ji Lang committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Lang, palace attendant and censor-in-chief, killed himself rather than see the surrender.

sentences.zh: 曜焚櫬受壁，使宋敞奉帝還宮。

translations.literal: Yao burned the bier, received the jade disk, and had Song Chang escort the emperor back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao burned the funeral bier, accepted the ritual jade, and sent Song Chang to convoy the emperor back inside.

sentences.zh: 初，有童謠曰：「天子何在豆田中。

translations.literal: At first there was a children’s rhyme that said, “Where is the Son of Heaven? In the bean fields.”
translations.idiomatic: A street rhyme had long asked where the emperor had gone—to “the beanfields.”

sentences.zh: 」時王浚在幽州，以豆有藿，殺隱士霍原以應之。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Jun was in Youzhou; because beans have pods (huo), he killed the recluse Huo Yuan to match the omen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun in Youzhou, playing at prophecy, murdered the hermit Huo Yuan because “bean” and “Huo” sounded alike.

sentences.zh: 及帝如曜營，營實在城東豆田壁。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Yao’s camp, the camp was in fact at the Dou field stockade east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the Jin ruler was driven to Liu Yao’s stockade at Doutian, east of Chang’an—exactly the “beanfield” the rhyme named.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，帝蒙塵于平陽，麹允及羣官並從。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the emperor suffered the dust of exile at Pingyang; Qu Yun and the host of officials all followed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the captive court reached Pingyang; Qu Yun and the ministers trailed behind in chains.

sentences.zh: 劉聰假帝光祿大夫、懷安侯。

translations.literal: Liu Cong gave the emperor the titular posts of Grand Master of Splendid Carriage and marquis of Huai’an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong ennobled him as marquis of Huai’an with a sinecure as grand master of splendid carriage.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，聰臨殿，帝稽首于前，麹允伏地慟哭，因自殺。

translations.literal: On renyin, Cong attended the hall; the emperor performed obeisance before him; Qu Yun lay on the ground wailing in grief and thereupon killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Next day at Liu Cong’s levee Sima Ye kowtowed while Qu Yun threw himself down, howled, and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 尚書梁允、侍中梁濬、散騎常侍嚴敦、左丞臧振、黃門侍郎任播、張偉、杜曼及諸郡守並爲曜所害，華輯奔南山。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Liang Yun, Palace Attendant Liang Jun, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Yan Dun, Left Assistant Cang Zhen, Attendant Gentlemen Ren Bo, Zhang Wei, Du Man, and the various grand administrators were all killed by Yao; Hua Ji fled to the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yun of the secretariat, Liang Jun at court, Yan Dun, Cang Zhen, Ren Bo, Zhang Wei, Du Man, and a string of local governors fell to Liu Yao’s executioners; only Hua Ji broke away toward the southern hills.

sentences.zh: 石勒圍樂平，司空劉琨遣兵援之，爲勒所敗，樂平太守韓據出奔。

translations.literal: Shi Le besieged Leping; Minister of Works Liu Kun sent troops to relieve it; they were defeated by Le; Grand Administrator of Leping Han Ju fled in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le ringed Leping; Liu Kun’s relief failed; Han Ju abandoned the city.

sentences.zh: 司空長史李弘以幷州叛，降于勒。

translations.literal: The chief clerk of the Minister of Works, Li Hong, rebelled in Bingzhou and surrendered to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong, chief clerk under Liu Kun, mutinied in Bingzhou and opened the province to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲申朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiashen it was the new moon; there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, new moon on jiashen: another eclipse of the sun.

sentences.zh: 己未，劉琨奔薊，依段匹磾。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Liu Kun fled to Ji and attached himself to Duan Pidi.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Liu Kun rode north to Ji to place himself under Duan Pidi’s protection.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月，帝在平陽。

translations.literal: In spring, first month of the fifth year, the emperor was at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth year began with the emperor still a hostage at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 庚子，虹霓彌天，三日並照。

translations.literal: On gengzi, rainbows filled the sky; three suns shone together.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi rainbows bridged the heavens and three suns glared at once—another ill omen.

sentences.zh: 平東將軍宋哲奔江左。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the East Song Zhe fled to the left of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhe gave up the north and ran south of the river.

sentences.zh: 李雄使其將李恭、羅寅寇巴東。

translations.literal: Li Xiong sent his generals Li Gong and Luo Yin to raid Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong ordered Li Gong and Luo Yin against Badong.

sentences.zh: 二月，劉聰使其將劉暢攻滎陽，太守李矩擊破之。

translations.literal: In the second month, Liu Cong sent his general Liu Chang to attack Xingyang; Grand Administrator Li Ju defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang’s column against Xingyang was smashed by Li Ju.

sentences.zh: 三月，琅邪王睿承制改元，稱晉王于建康。

translations.literal: In the third month, Prince Sima Rui of Langya, acting under interim authority, changed the reign title and styled himself Prince of Jin at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: at Jiankang Sima Rui of Langya assumed interim authority, adopted a new era name, and took the title Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 夏五月丙子，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In summer, fifth month, on bingzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fifth month, bingzi: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，大暑，司、冀、青、雍等四州螽蝗。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, there was great heat; Si, Ji, Qing, and Yong suffered from locusts and grasshoppers.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: a killing heat, while Si, Ji, Qing, and Yong swarmed with locusts and katydids.

sentences.zh: 石勒亦競取百姓禾，時人謂之「胡蝗」。

translations.literal: Shi Le likewise vied to seize the people’s grain; people of the time called it the “Hu locust.”
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le’s foragers stripped the fields so thoroughly that folk called them the “barbarian locust.”

sentences.zh: 八月，劉聰使趙固襲衛將軍華薈于定潁，遂害之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Liu Cong sent Zhao Gu to raid General of the Guard Hua Hui at Dingying and thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: Zhao Gu ambushed Hua Hui at Dingying and killed him.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙子，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, on bingzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, bingzi: eclipse.

sentences.zh: 劉聰出獵，令帝行車騎將軍，戎服執戟爲導，百姓聚而觀之，故老或歔欷流涕，聰聞而惡之。

translations.literal: Liu Cong went out hunting and ordered the emperor to act as General of Chariots and Cavalry, wearing military garb and holding a halberd to lead the way; the common people gathered to watch; some elders sighed and wept; Cong heard of it and detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong humiliated his captive by making him ride point in full armor at the hunt while crowds gawked; old men wept openly, and Liu Cong began to loathe him.

sentences.zh: 聰後因大會，使帝行酒洗爵，反而更衣，又使帝執蓋，晉臣在坐者多失聲而泣，尚書郎辛賓抱帝慟哭，爲聰所害。

translations.literal: Later, at a great gathering, Cong made the emperor pour wine and rinse cups; then he had him change clothes and hold an umbrella; many Jin ministers present could not restrain their sobs; Gentleman of the Secretariat Xin Bin embraced the emperor and wailed in grief, and Cong had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: At a later banquet he forced Sima Ye to wait tables, then hold a parasol over the revel; when Xin Bin clung to the emperor and wept, Liu Cong had him cut down.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊戌，帝遇弑，崩于平陽，時年十八。

translations.literal: On wuxu in the twelfth month, the emperor met assassination and died at Pingyang; he was eighteen sui.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu in the twelfth month Liu Cong’s assassins finished Sima Ye at Pingyang; he was eighteen.

sentences.zh: 帝之繼皇統也，屬永嘉之亂，天下崩離，長安城中戶不盈百，牆宇頹毀，蒿棘成林。

translations.literal: When the emperor succeeded to the imperial line, it fell amid the turmoil of Yongjia; the realm shattered and separated; in Chang’an city the households did not reach a hundred; walls and roofs were ruined and collapsed; wormwood and thorns grew into groves.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ye inherited the throne after Yongjia’s disaster: Chang’an held fewer than a hundred families, its battlements in ruins and thickets choking the lanes.

sentences.zh: 朝廷無車馬章服，唯桑版署號而已。

translations.literal: The court had no carriages, horses, or court robes; there were only mulwood boards on which titles were written.
translations.idiomatic: There were no carriages, seals, or silks—only names painted on mulberry planks for “offices.”

sentences.zh: 衆唯一旅，公私有車四乘，器械多闕，運饋不繼。

translations.literal: The host amounted to only one brigade; publicly and privately there were four carts; weapons were mostly lacking; transport of provisions did not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison was a single brigade, the palace could muster four carts, arsenals stood empty, and supply trains never arrived.

sentences.zh: 巨猾滔天，帝京危急，諸侯無釋位之志，征鎮闕勤王之舉，故君臣窘迫，以至殺辱云。

translations.literal: Monstrous villains rose to heaven; the imperial capital was in desperate peril; the feudal lords had no mind to vacate their posts; the commanders on the marches lacked the will to rescue the king; therefore ruler and minister were driven to extremity until slaughter and humiliation ensued.
translations.idiomatic: While rebels towered like a flood and the capital starved, no prince stirred from his fief and no general marched to the rescue—so sovereign and minister were cornered into surrender, insult, and death.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔炎暉杪暮，英雄多假于宗室。

translations.literal: The historians say: In old days when the flame of Han guttered low, heroes often borrowed strength from the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The annalists remark that at the twilight of Han, power had leaned heavily on imperial kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 金德韜華，顛沛共推于懷愍。

translations.literal: When the virtue of metal hid its brilliance, overturn and wandering were alike thrust upon Emperors Huai and Min.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin’s “metal” virtue dimmed, both Huai and Min inherited collapse.

sentences.zh: 樊陽寂寥，兵車靡會，豈力不足而情有餘乎？

translations.literal: Fanyang stood silent; war-chariots never mustered—was it that strength was lacking while feeling ran deep?
translations.idiomatic: Armies never linked at Fanyang—was it mere weakness, or something worse?

sentences.zh: 喋喋遺萌，苟存其主，譬彼詩人，愛其棠樹。

translations.literal: Chattering survivors clung to their lord as the poets loved the pear-trees of the hall of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The rump court clung to its prince the way the ode clung to the lord of Shao’s pear-trees.

sentences.zh: 夫有非常之事，而無非常之功，詳觀發迹，用非天啓，是以輿棺齒劍，可得而言焉。

translations.literal: Yet when there are extraordinary events without extraordinary achievements, examining how power arose shows it was not Heaven’s opening—therefore one may speak of bearing the bier between one’s teeth and facing the sword.
translations.idiomatic: Extraordinary crisis met no extraordinary response; tracing how authority ebbed shows no mandate of Heaven—only the shame of surrender, coffin and jade between the teeth.

sentences.zh: 于時五嶽三塗，並皆淪寇，龍州、牛首，故以立君。

translations.literal: At that time the Five Marchmounts and the Three Passes alike sank into banditry; Longzhou and Ox-Head were reasons enough to set up a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Every sacred peak and every choke-point had fallen to invaders; omens at Longzhou and Ox-Head were cited to justify enthroning a boy on the run.

sentences.zh: 股肱非挑戰之秋，劉石有滔天之勢，療饑中斷，嬰戈外絕，兩京淪狄，再駕徂戎。

translations.literal: The arms and thighs were no match for the season of challenge; Liu and Shi possessed momentum that drowned the sky; famine medicine was cut off in mid-course, spears were broken off abroad; both capitals fell to Di, twice the imperial carriage marched out to war.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty’s limbs were unfit for battle while Liu Yuan and Shi Le swelled like a flood; relief failed within, allies failed without; Luoyang and Chang’an fell to barbarians, and two emperors rode out to disaster.

sentences.zh: 周王隕首於驪峰，衛公亡肝於淇上，思爲一郡，其可得乎！

translations.literal: The Zhou king lost his head on Mount Li; the duke of Wei lost his liver on the Qi—who could hope to be even one commandery in such an hour!
translations.idiomatic: They likened the age to King You’s end at Li Mountain and the martyr duke of Wei on the Qi—no one could pretend a single prefecture would suffice.

sentences.zh: 干寶有言曰：

translations.literal: Gan Bao has said:
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao observed:

sentences.zh: 昔高祖宣皇帝以雄才碩量，應時而仕，值魏太祖創基之初，籌畫軍國，嘉謀屢中，遂服輿軫，驅馳三世。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Xuan the August, with heroic talent and great capacity, answered the times and entered office; he met the founding of Wei by Emperor Wu of Wei; he planned for army and state; his fine strategies repeatedly hit the mark; therefore he mounted the chariot shafts and galloped through three reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi rose under Cao Cao with genius enough to steer three reigns of Wei.

sentences.zh: 性深阻有若城府，而能寬綽以容納；

translations.literal: His nature was deep and obstructed like a city wall, yet he could be broad and easy in tolerating others;
translations.idiomatic: He seemed all moats and battlements within, yet he could embrace men generously;

sentences.zh: 行任數以御物，而知人善采拔。

translations.literal: he acted by calculation to control things, yet he knew men and was good at selecting and promoting them.
translations.idiomatic: he governed by stratagem but knew talent and promoted it well;

sentences.zh: 故賢愚咸懷，大小畢力。

translations.literal: Therefore the worthy and the foolish alike cherished him, great and small alike exerted their strength.
translations.idiomatic: so clever and simple alike served him loyally.

sentences.zh: 爾乃取鄧艾于農隙，引州泰於行役，委以文武，各善其事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Deng Ai from a farm recess and brought Zhou Tai from corvée labor, entrusting them with civil and military affairs, each excelling in his task.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled Deng Ai from the furrows and Zhou Tai from labor gangs and gave each a command that fitted him.

sentences.zh: 故能西禽孟達，東舉公孫，內夷曹爽，外襲王淩。

translations.literal: Therefore he was able to take Meng Da alive in the west, raise Gongsun in the east, pacify Cao Shuang within, and strike Wang Ling without.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he seized Meng Da, broke Gongsun Yuan, destroyed Cao Shuang, and ambushed Wang Ling.

sentences.zh: 神略獨斷，征伐四克，維御羣后，大權在己。

translations.literal: With divine strategy and independent decisions, his expeditions conquered on every side; he maintained the host of lords and great power rested in himself.
translations.idiomatic: His campaigns succeeded by ruthless calculation until all power sat in his hands.

sentences.zh: 于是百姓與能，大象始構。

translations.literal: Thereupon the hundred surnnames granted him their allegiance, and the great image began to take form.
translations.idiomatic: The people accepted his rule and the Sima edifice rose.

sentences.zh: 世宗承基，太祖繼業，玄豐亂內，欽誕寇外，潛謀雖密，而在機必兆；

translations.literal: Shizong inherited the foundation, Taizu continued the enterprise; Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin raised rebellion within the realm, Zhuge Dan and Wen Yang campaigned against the court from the Huai region—though secret plots ran deep, whenever the crisis came an omen had already appeared;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming and Emperor Wu carried the Sima mandate forward even as Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin convulsed the interior and Zhuge Dan with Wen Yang shook the Huai frontier—each conspiracy, for all its secrecy, had bled warning signs long before it broke.

sentences.zh: 淮浦再擾，而許洛不震：咸黜異圖，用融前烈。

translations.literal: the Huai shore was twice disturbed, yet Xu and Luo did not tremble: they all dismissed alien designs and thereby continued the earlier merit.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan rose twice, yet the heartland held because dissent was crushed early.

sentences.zh: 然後推轂鐘鄧，長驅庸蜀，三關電埽，而劉禪入臣，天符人事，於是信矣。

translations.literal: Then they pushed the chariot wheels for Zhong and Deng, drove straight into Shu, swept the three passes like lightning, and Liu Shan entered as a subject—Heaven’s tally and human affairs at that point were credible.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui and Deng Ai opened Shu; the three passes fell like lightning; Liu Shan surrendered—proof that Heaven and men favored the Simas.

sentences.zh: 始當非常之禮，終受備物之錫。

translations.literal: At first they received extraordinary rites; in the end they received the full regalia of investiture.
translations.idiomatic: They began with extraordinary honors and ended with the full imperial regalia.

sentences.zh: 至于世祖，遂享皇極。

translations.literal: As for Shizu, he then enjoyed the supreme throne.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu at last took the throne.

sentences.zh: 仁以厚下，儉以足用，和而不弛，寬而能斷，故民詠維新，四海悅勸矣。

translations.literal: With benevolence to enrich those below, with frugality to make supplies sufficient, harmonious yet not lax, lenient yet able to decide—therefore the people sang of renewal and within the four seas all were glad and encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with kindness, thrift, balance, and firm judgment until the empire sang of renewal.

sentences.zh: 聿修祖宗之志，思輯戰國之苦。

translations.literal: He took up the intent of his ancestors and thought to bind up the sufferings of the Warring States era.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to heal the wounds of the long wars.

sentences.zh: 腹心不同，公卿異議，而獨納羊祜之策，杖王杜之決，役不二時，江湘來同。

translations.literal: Though hearts in the center differed and dukes and ministers disputed, he alone adopted Yang Hu’s plan, relied on the decisions of Wang and Du, and within two seasons’ labor the Yangzi and Xiang came over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Despite divided councils he followed Yang Hu and Wang Jun, and in two campaigns Wu fell.

sentences.zh: 掩唐虞之舊域，班正朔於八荒，天下書同文，車同軌，牛馬被野，餘糧委畝，故于時有「天下無窮人」之諺。

translations.literal: He covered the old domain of Tang and Yu, extended the correct calendar to the eight wilds; under Heaven writing was the same script, carts the same track; cattle and horses covered the wilderness, surplus grain lay in the fields—therefore at that time there was the proverb “Under Heaven there are no destitute people.”
translations.idiomatic: He restored the ancient heartland, unified script and axle-width, filled the fields with grain and herds—so men said there were no beggars in the realm.

sentences.zh: 雖太平未洽，亦足以明吏奉其法，民樂其生矣。

translations.literal: Although perfect peace was not yet everywhere, it was still enough to show that officials upheld the law and the people delighted in their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Even if perfect peace never arrived, officials still obeyed the code and commoners still trusted their lives to it.

sentences.zh: 武皇旣崩，山陵未乾，而楊駿被誅，母后廢黜。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu had passed away, the mausoleum mound was not yet dry when Yang Jun was executed and the empress dowager was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly was Wu’s tomb sealed when Yang Jun died and the empress mother was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 尋以二公、楚王之變，宗子無維城之助，師尹無具瞻之貴，至乃易天子乙太上之號，而有免官之謠。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, with the changes involving the two dukes and the Prince of Chu, imperial sons lacked the “walling city” of support; ministers of state lacked the dignity of universal regard—to the point of changing the Son of Heaven’s title to that of supreme emperor, while ballads spoke of dismissed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the coup of the “two dukes” and the Prince of Chu: no prince buttressed the throne, no chief minister commanded respect, titles turned mockeries, and street songs mocked dismissed grandees.

sentences.zh: 民不見德，惟亂是聞，朝爲伊周，夕成桀蹠，善惡陷於成敗，毀譽脅於世利，內外混淆，庶官失才，名實反錯，天綱解紐。

translations.literal: The people saw no virtue, they heard only of chaos; in the morning men were Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, by evening they were Jie and Robber Zhi; good and evil sank into success and failure, praise and blame were twisted by worldly profit; inside and outside were confused, the hundred offices lost their proper talents, name and reality were reversed, and Heaven’s net came undone.
translations.idiomatic: Morals inverted overnight; office became a lottery of profit; inside and outside the court no one matched his title, and the bonds of order snapped.

sentences.zh: 國政迭移於亂人，禁兵外散于四方，方岳無鈞石之鎮，關門無結草之固。

translations.literal: State power passed in turn to villains; palace guards were scattered to the four quarters; regional commanders lacked the weight of stone anchors; passes lacked even the defense of tied grass.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels seized the levers of power, imperial guards were farmed out, governors had no real armies, and frontier gates stood open.

sentences.zh: 李辰、石冰傾之於荊楊，元海、王彌撓之於青冀，戎羯稱制，二帝失尊，何哉？

translations.literal: Li Chen and Shi Bing overturned Jing and Yang; Yuanhai and Wang Mi harassed Qing and Ji; Rong and Jie seized the reins; the two emperors lost their majesty—why?
translations.idiomatic: Li Chen and Shi Bing wrecked the southeast, Liu Yuan and Wang Mi the northeast; Xiongnu and Jie took command while two Jin emperors lost their throne—why?

sentences.zh: 樹立失權，託付非才，四維不張，而苟且之政多也。

translations.literal: Because the tree of authority had been planted awry, the charge was given to unworthy hands, the four bonds were not stretched tight, and makeshift expedients multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Because power had been rooted in the wrong men, talent was mismatched to office, the four social ties hung slack, and patchwork policy piled on patchwork policy.

sentences.zh: 夫作法於治，其弊猶亂；

translations.literal: When you make law in an age of order, its defects may still bring chaos;
translations.idiomatic: Institutions framed in order can still decay into chaos;

sentences.zh: 作法於亂，誰能救之！

translations.literal: when you make law in an age of chaos, who can save it!
translations.idiomatic: but institutions born from chaos cannot be mended by anyone.

sentences.zh: 彼元海者，離石之將兵都尉；

translations.literal: That Liu Yuan was a commandant of troops at Lishi;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan was only a garrison captain at Lishi;

sentences.zh: 王彌者，青州之散吏也。

translations.literal: Wang Mi was a petty clerk in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi a minor scribbler in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 蓋皆弓馬之士，驅走之人，非有吳先主、諸葛孔明之能也；

translations.literal: They were altogether men of bow and horse, drivers and runners; they did not have the abilities of the Wu liege or Zhuge Kongming;
translations.idiomatic: They were horsemen and runners, not Liu Bei or Zhuge Liang;

sentences.zh: 新起之寇，烏合之衆，非吳蜀之敵也；

translations.literal: rising bandits, flocks of crows—not enemies fit for Wu or Shu;
translations.idiomatic: their hosts were new-minted rabble, no match for Wu or Shu veterans;

sentences.zh: 脫耒爲兵，裂裳爲旗，非戰國之器也；

translations.literal: they cast aside ploughs for weapons and tore robes for banners—not the armament of the Warring States;
translations.idiomatic: they grabbed hoes for spears and rags for flags—no Warring States arsenal;

sentences.zh: 自下逆上，非鄰國之勢也。

translations.literal: they struck upward from below—not the posture of neighboring states at odds.
translations.idiomatic: they were peasants turned upside down, not rival kingdoms of old.

sentences.zh: 然而擾天下如驅羣羊，舉二都如拾遺芥，將相王侯連頸以受戮，后嬪妃主虜辱於戎卒，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Yet they disturbed all under Heaven as if driving a flock of sheep, took the two capitals as easily as picking up stray husks; generals, ministers, kings, and marquises yielded their necks to execution; empresses and consorts suffered outrage at the hands of barbarian soldiers—is it not pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Yet such men herded the realm like sheep, pocketed both capitals like chaff, strung up the entire nobility, and outraged the women of the palace—how bitter a sight!

sentences.zh: 天下，大器也；

translations.literal: All under Heaven is a great vessel;
translations.idiomatic: The empire is a great vessel;

sentences.zh: 羣生，重畜也。

translations.literal: the myriad living are a heavy herd.
translations.idiomatic: the people are a weighty herd.

sentences.zh: 愛惡相攻，利害相奪，其勢常也。

translations.literal: Love and hate strike one another, profit and harm wrest from one another—that tendency is constant.
translations.idiomatic: Love contends with hate, gain with loss—that tension never rests.

sentences.zh: 若積水于防，燎火于原，未嘗暫靜也。

translations.literal: It is like storing water behind a dike or setting fire on a plain—it has never for a moment been still.
translations.idiomatic: It is water pent behind a levee or flame on dry grass—never still.

sentences.zh: 器大者，不可以小道治；

translations.literal: A great vessel cannot be governed by petty ways;
translations.idiomatic: A great realm cannot be ruled by petty tricks;

sentences.zh: 勢重者，不可以爭競擾。

translations.literal: a heavy situation cannot be disturbed by wrangling for advantage.
translations.idiomatic: a grave crisis cannot survive factional greed.

sentences.zh: 古先哲王知其然也，是以扞其大患，禦其大災。

translations.literal: The sage kings of antiquity knew this; therefore they warded off great calamity and controlled great disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sages knew it, and so they met great peril with great remedies.

sentences.zh: 百姓皆知上德之生己，而不謂浚己以生也，是以感而應之，悅而歸之，如晨風之鬱北林，龍魚之趣藪澤也。

translations.literal: The hundred surnnames all knew that the sovereign’s virtue gave them life, and did not think that he squeezed them to live himself; therefore they were moved and responded, were glad and returned to him, as morning wind thickens the northern forest, as dragons and fish hasten to the marsh.
translations.idiomatic: When the people believe the throne nurtures rather than drains them, they rally as fish to deep water or wind to the grove.

sentences.zh: 然後設禮文以理之，斷刑罰以威之，謹好惡以示之，審禍福以喻之，求明察以官之，尊慈愛以固之。

translations.literal: Then he sets ritual pattern to order them, applies punishments to awe them, clarifies likes and dislikes to show them, examines fortune and disaster to instruct them, seeks clear insight to officer them, honors loving kindness to consolidate them.
translations.idiomatic: Then rites teach, punishments warn, examples guide, fortune and misfortune are explained, wise officers appointed, and mercy shown to bind hearts.

sentences.zh: 故衆知向方，皆樂其生而哀其死，悅其教而安其俗；

translations.literal: Therefore the multitude knows the direction to turn; all rejoice in life and mourn death; they delight in his teaching and rest secure in his customs;
translations.idiomatic: The people know where to turn: they cherish life, honor death, trust his teaching, and settle in his ways;

sentences.zh: 君子勤禮，小人盡力，廉恥篤於家閭，邪辟消於胸懷。

translations.literal: the gentleman is diligent in ritual, the petty man exhausts his strength; integrity is thick in hamlet and lane, and perverse thoughts vanish from the breast.
translations.idiomatic: gentlemen polish conduct, commoners give their strength, shame roots in every lane, and wicked thoughts fade.

sentences.zh: 故其民有見危以授命，而不求生以害義，又況可奮臂大呼，聚之以干紀作亂乎！

translations.literal: Therefore among his people there are those who, seeing peril, will give their lives and will not seek life by harming righteousness—how much less would they wave their arms and shout, gathering to violate the norm and raise rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: So men will die for duty rather than live by betraying it—let alone riot for private ends!

sentences.zh: 基廣則難傾，根深則難拔，理節則不亂，膠結則不遷，是以昔之有天下者之所以長久也。

translations.literal: When the base is broad it is hard to overturn; when the roots are deep they are hard to uproot; when principle is ordered there is no chaos; when things are glued fast they do not shift—that is why those who formerly possessed all under Heaven lasted long.
translations.idiomatic: Broad foundations, deep roots, clear principle, firm bonds—that is how old dynasties endured.

sentences.zh: 夫豈無僻主，賴道德典刑以維持之也。

translations.literal: It is not that there were no depraved lords; they relied on moral power and model punishments to sustain them.
translations.idiomatic: Even weak rulers endured when ritual and law still held.

sentences.zh: 昔周之興也，後稷生於姜嫄，而天命昭顯，文武之功起於后稷。

translations.literal: In olden days when the Zhou arose, Hou Ji was born of Jiang Yuan, and Heaven’s mandate shone bright; the merit of Kings Wen and Wu took its rise from Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou line began with Hou Ji, child of Jiang Yuan, when Heaven’s favor was already plain—the martial kings only completed what he started.

sentences.zh: 至於公劉，遭夏人之亂，去邰之豳，身服厥勞。

translations.literal: As for Gong Liu, he met the disorders of the Xia people, left Tai for Bin, and wore the toil on his own body.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Liu fled Xia turmoil from Tai to Bin and bore every hardship himself.

sentences.zh: 至於太王，爲戎翟所逼，而不忍百姓之命，杖策而去之。

translations.literal: As for Tai Wang, pressed by the Rong and Di, yet unable to endure the risk to the common people, he took his staff and left them.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Wang abandoned the valley rather than sacrifice his people to the Rong and Di.

sentences.zh: 故從之如歸市，一年成邑，二年成都，三年五倍其初。

translations.literal: Therefore they followed him as if hurrying to market; in one year it became a town, in two a city, in three it was fivefold what it had been at first.
translations.idiomatic: The clans flocked after him; within three years his settlement had grown fivefold.

sentences.zh: 至於王季，能貊其德音；

translations.literal: As for Wang Ji, he could extend his virtuous repute.
translations.idiomatic: King Ji carried his virtuous name to the border peoples.

sentences.zh: 至于文王，而維新其命。

translations.literal: as for King Wen, he renewed the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen renewed Heaven’s charge to the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，周家世積忠厚，仁及草木，內隆九族，外尊事黃耇，以成其福祿者也。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, the House of Zhou for generations piled up honesty and generous goodness, extending benevolence even to grass and trees, promoting kin within the nine degrees, honoring gray-haired elders without—thereby completing their blessing and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Generation after generation the Zhou stored up loyalty and kindness, care for kin and respect for age, until fortune itself answered their virtue.

sentences.zh: 而其妃后躬行四教，尊敬師傅，服瀚濯之衣，修煩辱之事，化天下以成婦道。

translations.literal: Their consorts and queens personally practiced the four womanly teachings, honored tutors and teachers, wore coarse washed garments, and took on troublesome, humble tasks, transforming all under Heaven to perfect the way of wives.
translations.idiomatic: Their queens modeled the four virtues, dressed plainly, worked at women’s tasks, and set the standard for every household.

sentences.zh: 是以漢濱之女，守潔白之志，中林之士，有純一之德，始於憂勤，終於逸樂。

translations.literal: Therefore the girls along the Han kept chaste resolve, and gentlemen in the groves held pure, single-minded virtue; they began in anxious toil and ended in ease and joy.
translations.idiomatic: So maidens by the Han kept their honor and recluses their integrity, moving from hardship to peace.

sentences.zh: 以三聖之知，伐獨夫之紂，猶正其名教，曰逆取順守。

translations.literal: With the wisdom of the three sages they attacked the lone tyrant Zhou, yet they still rectified the teaching of moral names, calling it “take by rebellion, keep by submission.”
translations.idiomatic: Even when the sage kings overthrew Di Xin, they framed the deed in classical language—conquest as correction.

sentences.zh: 及周公遭變，陳后稷先公風化之所由，致王業之艱難者，則皆農夫女工衣蝕之事也。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Zhou met with calamity, he set forth how the transforming influence of Hou Ji and the former dukes arose, and what made the royal enterprise difficult—matters all of farmers’ and weavers’ worn clothing.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou’s admonitions traced royal legitimacy through furrow and loom, not through idle pomp.

sentences.zh: 故自后之始基靖民，十五王而文始平之，十六王而武始居之，十八王而康克安之。

translations.literal: Therefore from Hou Ji’s first settling the people, through fifteen kings Wen first brought peace, through sixteen kings Wu first dwelt there, through eighteen kings Kang was able to secure them.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicle counts kings from Hou Ji to Wen, Wu, and Kang—each reign laying another layer of order.

sentences.zh: 故其積基樹本，經緯禮俗，節理人情，恤隱民事，如此之纏緜也。

translations.literal: Therefore they piled foundation and planted root, wove warp and weft of ritual and custom, regulated human feeling, and pitied the hidden troubles of the people—care as tangled and continuous as this.
translations.idiomatic: That is how Zhou built a state: patient attention to ritual, sentiment, and the livelihood of the meanest subject.

sentences.zh: 今晉之興也，功烈於百王，事捷於三代。

translations.literal: Now as Jin arose, its deeds outshone the hundred kings and its affairs were swifter than those of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s rise was swifter and more dazzling than Xia, Shang, or Zhou.

sentences.zh: 宣景遭多難之時，誅庶孽以便事，不及修公劉、太王之仁也。

translations.literal: Emperors Xuan and Jing lived through repeated crises, executing collateral lines for political convenience—they had no leisure to cultivate the benevolence of a Gong Liu or Tai Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi and Sima Shi cut down rivals for expediency; they could not pause to mimic Zhou’s slow nurturing of the people.

sentences.zh: 受遺輔政，屢遇廢置，故齊王不明，不獲思庸於亳；

translations.literal: Receiving the testamentary charge to assist the government, they repeatedly faced deposition and installation; therefore the Prince of Qi was unenlightened and could not “think of worthies at Bo”;
translations.idiomatic: Regency meant endless coups: Sima Jiong of Qi proved a poor steward, nothing like the Duke of Zhou at Boqin;

sentences.zh: 高貴沖人，不得復子明辟也。

translations.literal: the noble and elevated ruler was a mere child and could never again receive the bright charge of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mao, the “noble and elevated” emperor, was only a boy-tragedy and never truly ruled.

sentences.zh: 二祖逼禪代之期，不暇待參分八百之會也。

translations.literal: The two Founders pressed the moment of forced abdication and had no time to wait for the leisurely “three parts in eight hundred” covenant of old.
translations.idiomatic: The two Sima founders hurried the Wei–Jin transition; they could not wait on ancient ritual niceties.

sentences.zh: 是其創基立本，異於先代者也。

translations.literal: This is how their founding of the base and planting of the root differed from earlier dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Their foundation was laid in haste and steel, not in Zhou-style patience.

sentences.zh: 加以朝寡純德之人，鄉乏不貳之老，風俗淫僻，恥尚失所，學者以老莊爲宗而黜《六經》，談者以虛蕩爲辨而賤名檢，行身者以放濁爲通而狹節信，進仕者以苟得爲貴而鄙居正，當官者以望空爲高而笑勤恪。

translations.literal: Add to that: at court few were of pure virtue; in the hamlets none were steadfast elders; customs ran licentious and depraved, standards of shame and honor collapsed; scholars took Laozi and Zhuangzi as orthodoxy and cast aside the Six Classics; debaters prized hollow cleverness and despised name and restraint; those who cultivated the self called dissipation “penetration” and narrowed integrity and good faith; those who sought office prized opportunistic gain and scorned upright living; those who held posts took vacant posturing for high-mindedness and laughed at diligent conscientiousness.
translations.idiomatic: Worse followed: court and countryside alike abandoned classical restraint—Qingtan wit replaced the Odes, cynicism replaced integrity, and office became a scramble for place.

sentences.zh: 是以劉頌屢言治道，傅咸每糾邪正，皆謂之俗吏；

translations.literal: Therefore when Liu Song repeatedly discoursed on good government, and Fu Xian repeatedly corrected wrong and right, they were all labeled vulgar clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song’s policy papers and Fu Xian’s moral lectures earned only the sneer “petty official”;

sentences.zh: 其倚杖虛曠，依阿無心者皆名重海內。

translations.literal: while those who leaned on empty vastness and clung without principle won fame throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: men who drifted through conversation without conviction were hailed as sages.

sentences.zh: 若夫文王日旰不暇食，仲山甫夙夜匪懈者，蓋共嗤黜以爲灰塵矣。

translations.literal: As for a King Wen who had no leisure to eat till dusk, or a Zhong Shanfu who never slackened day or night—the crowd scorned them as dust and ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Diligence like King Wen’s or Zhong Shanfu’s drew mockery, not respect.

sentences.zh: 由是毀譽亂于善惡之實，情慝奔于貨欲之塗。

translations.literal: Hence praise and blame no longer matched true good and evil; secret passions all ran toward greed.
translations.idiomatic: Reputation parted from reality, and every heart chased profit.

sentences.zh: 選者爲人擇官，官者爲身擇利，而執鈞當軸之士，身兼官以十數。

translations.literal: Those who dispensed office chose posts for patrons; those who held office chose profit for themselves; men at the hub of power personally accumulated a dozen titles.
translations.idiomatic: Patronage sold posts; incumbents sold favors; grandees stacked ten offices on one back.

sentences.zh: 大極其尊，小錄其耍，而世族貴戚之子弟，陵邁超越，不拘資次。

translations.literal: The greatest seized the loftiest rank, the petty clutched whatever leverage they could, while sons of great clans vaulted over proper seniority without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Great families leapfrogged the queue while small fry grabbed any scrap of authority.

sentences.zh: 悠悠風塵，皆奔競之士，列官千百，無讓賢之舉。

translations.literal: Endless in wind and dust, all were men racing for place; offices numbered in the thousands, yet none yielded to worthier men.
translations.idiomatic: The roads swelled with office-seekers, yet no one stepped aside for talent.

sentences.zh: 子真著《崇讓》而莫之省，子雅制九班而不得用。

translations.literal: Liu Shi, courtesy name Zizhen, wrote “Exalting Yielding,” yet none took it to heart; Liu Song, courtesy name Ziya, framed the Nine Ranks, yet it could not be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi’s essay on yielding and Liu Song’s nine-grade reform were ignored in practice.

sentences.zh: 其婦女，莊櫛織紝皆取成於婢僕，未嘗知女工絲枲之業，中饋酒蝕之事也。

translations.literal: As for their women, rouge, combs, and weaving were all left to maids; they never knew women’s work in silk and hemp, or the inner kitchen’s labor of wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: Ladies knew only slaves’ labor for their finery and never touched loom or kettle.

sentences.zh: 先時而婚，任情而動，故皆不恥淫泆之過，不拘妒忌之惡，父兄不之罪也，天下莫之非也。

translations.literal: They married early and followed impulse; none blushed at promiscuity, none feared jealousy’s stigma—fathers and brothers did not punish them, and the world raised no blame.
translations.idiomatic: Early marriage and open intrigue drew no rebuke from kin or gossip from neighbors.

sentences.zh: 又況責之聞四教於古，修貞順於今，以輔佐君子者哉！

translations.literal: How much less could one expect them to hear the four teachings of antiquity and cultivate chaste submission today in order to assist their husbands!
translations.idiomatic: Who could demand of them the classical wife’s virtues?

sentences.zh: 禮法刑政於此大壞，如水斯積而決其提防，如火斯畜而離其薪燎也。

translations.literal: Rites, law, punishment, and government were thus broken—as water that pools until the dike bursts, as fire that gathers until it leaves the woodpile.
translations.idiomatic: Law and ritual collapsed like a dammed flood or a stacked bonfire breaking loose.

sentences.zh: 國之將亡，未必先顛，其此之謂乎！

translations.literal: A state need not topple first at the root when it is about to perish—is this not the meaning!
translations.idiomatic: Dynasties rot from within long before the walls fall—so it was here.

sentences.zh: 故觀阮籍之行，而覺禮教崩馳之所由也。

translations.literal: Therefore observe Ruan Ji’s conduct, and you see why moral instruction collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: One has only to read Ruan Ji’s life to see how teaching of the rites unraveled.

sentences.zh: 察庾純、賈充之爭，而見師尹之多僻；

translations.literal: Examine the quarrel of Yu Chun and Jia Chong, and you see how chief ministers were mostly crooked.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu–Jia feud exposed the moral bankruptcy of the high ministers.

sentences.zh: 考平吳之功，而知將帥之不讓；

translations.literal: Consider the merit claimed in pacifying Wu, and you know the generals would not yield to one another.
translations.idiomatic: The conquest of Wu showed commanders scrambling for credit, not glory shared.

sentences.zh: 思郭欽之謀，而寤戎狄之有釁；

translations.literal: Ponder Guo Qin’s memorial, and you wake to the opening the Rong and Di were given.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qin had warned that barbarians on the border would devour Jin if left unchecked.

sentences.zh: 覽傅玄、劉毅之言，而得百官之邪；

translations.literal: Read Fu Xuan’s and Liu Yi’s memorials, and you grasp the perversity of the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan and Liu Yi laid bare official corruption in plain words.

sentences.zh: 核傅咸之奏、《錢神》之論，而𧡺寵賂之彰。

translations.literal: Study Fu Xian’s submissions and the “Money God” essay, and you see how blatant favor and bribery had become.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian’s court papers and Lu Bao’s satire showed bribery ruling every appointment.

sentences.zh: 民風國勢如此，雖以中庸之才，守文之主治之，辛有必見之於祭祀，季劄必得之於聲樂，范燮必爲之請死，賈誼必爲之痛哭，又況我惠帝以放蕩之德臨之哉！

translations.literal: With popular temper and state strength in such a case, even a middling talent and a conserving ruler could not have governed them—Xin You would have read it in the sacrifices, Ji Zha in the music, Fan Xie would have begged death, Jia Yi would have wept aloud—and how much more when Emperor Hui sat above them with dissolute virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Even a mediocre caretaker could not have saved such a polity; the omens were as plain as in Xin You’s day—and Emperor Hui was no caretaker.

sentences.zh: 懷帝承亂得位，羈於強臣，愍帝奔播之後，徒廁其虛名，天下之政旣去，非命世之雄才，不能取之矣！

translations.literal: Emperor Huai inherited chaos and was tethered by strong ministers; after Emperor Min’s flight he merely held an empty title—government had slipped away, and without a hero of the age none could recover it!
translations.idiomatic: Huai was a prisoner of warlords, Min a refugee with a hollow crown; only a world-shaking champion could have picked up the pieces.

sentences.zh: 淳耀之烈未渝，故大命重集於中宗元皇帝。

translations.literal: The bright flame was not yet extinguished; therefore the Great Mandate gathered again on Zhongzong, Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s fire still smoldered in the south, where Yuan Di refounded the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：懷佩玉璽，愍居黃屋。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Huai bore the jade seals; Min occupied the yellow canopy.
translations.idiomatic: The verse runs: Huai clasped the imperial jade; Min mounted the yellow-canopied cart of state.

sentences.zh: 鼈墜三山，鯨吞九服，獯入金商，穹居未央。

translations.literal: The tortoise fell from Three Mountains; the whale swallowed the nine domains; the Xiongnu entered the Jinyin and Shang gates; nomad tents rose in Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Portent and disaster: omens failed, invaders filled the palace wards, and steppe rulers sat in the Han halls.

sentences.zh: 圜顱盡仆，方趾咸僵。

translations.literal: Round heads toppled, square toes stiffened—all lay dead.
translations.idiomatic: Every class of subject fell—none escaped the slaughter.

sentences.zh: 大夫反首，徙我平陽。

translations.literal: Great officers with disheveled heads were herded off to our Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bound nobles were marched to captivity in Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 主憂臣哭，于何不臧！

translations.literal: The lord mourned, his ministers wept—where was the good in it!
translations.idiomatic: Sovereign and servant wept together—what blessing could remain?
